Not only that, but insisted on making small talk as my friend stood against the oven, and he leaned against the sink in our small kitchen.

It was about three o’clock in the afternoon and I had yet to leave my house, nor did I have any particular plans to. Not only that but I was getting mighty hungry. So when my date from the previous week called me and then texted me that he was at a burrito place and wanted to bring over a burrito and his apparently new girlfriend Sarah, it seemed a little silly to say no, even though I hadn’t had a very good time on the date with him the first time and hadn’t really planned to go on any more with him. But his girlfriend was coming, so I figured there was no way he could try to hook up with me. Besides, didn’t I always say I wanted to make some girlfriends in Portland?

We went to the park with our burritos because we also wanted to drink the lovely dark six-pack they’d brought and my house was one of sobriety, as I may have mentioned previously. We went to Brooklyn Park which, despite being two blocks from my house, I had never visited. We sat at a picnic table near the edge of the park — underneath the sky which was slowly fading to night. Sarah and I found that we had a few things in common: we were both from LA, we both liked photography, and our parents had encouraged us to follow similar paths in our lives. Then Robin apparently felt he wasn’t getting enough attention so we changed the topic to one that could include him — astrology. After that we talked about various games we’d played as children — such as Thomas the Tank Engine, and about becoming artists in Portland. I got the feeling Robin wanted to remind me of the connection we had, and didn’t seem to like that Sarah and I seemed to be hitting it off without him.

When it became dark enough that we had trouble seeing, we returned to my house and, as it often seemed to, the subject of online dating came up. I hadn’t met any other girls who were familiar to the site, so I asked her some basic questions about her use of it, and she told me that she didn’t really need to message anyone since she got about five messages per day and Robin and I (but secretly) were surprised, both thinking that, being an attractive girl, she had to receive more. It was hard to compare as I’d become accustomed to sending first messages to anyone who looked remotely appealing, but I couldn’t remember getting that many messages.

In the time we’d been talking, Robin and Sarah had converged on the couch in our living room, while I pulled my black rolly chair over so I was seated in front of them. I began to feel like a therapist as the topic of their relationship came up and I crossed my legs and pursed my lips. It seemed an unresolved quandary in both of their minds. They’d gone to a mountain together the night before and had worked out that they wanted a relationship after all, even though in the past Sarah hadn’t completely been on board for monogamy, and then Robin had done something to, well anyway, they were trying to figure out what label to have. As they talked, they settled comfortably into lying next to each other, and I maintained my role, asking pertinent questions, but mostly just listening and making sure they each had a chance to speak.

I made sure that they both got their voice heard, while staying as unbiased as possible, which was pretty unbiased since I couldn’t really figure any opinion to have about the situation. I wasn’t clear on the exact particular reason why Sarah would choose Robin in the first place, and that may have been a missing link in trying to figure out what should go on in the future.

At any rate, after they both had a chance to talk, they seemed to have resolved something, and I hurriedly got back to tinder so I could find a date to match their level of cuddliness. I arranged for a Mr. Blake Bamford to come over and he asked if I wanted him to pick anything up on the way, so I said a small can of beer. When he arrived, I went out to meet him in his car and it emerged that he had for some reason chosen to wear different shades of fluorescent clothing. I wondered if I should discreetly ask if he had just come from, or was planning on going to, a rave, but thought better of it and simply ushered him inside my house.

I introduced him to everyone and, as you might imagine, awkwardness ensued. Though we’d already crossed the material boundary of the curtain which separated the living room from the kitchen, I asked him if he wanted me to make him tea, and tried to, thinking it was about time I become something more like a lady, except that I didn’t put the teapot on the right burner, and the longer we waited the longer absolutely nothing happened. He got the impression, after I told him that I was a dancer because I had taken two modern dance classes in college, that I was a slightly different kind of dancer. Portland is known for its strip clubs — so I had to clarify this. And it was precisely as I was clarifying this that my roommate emerged from his other room into the kitchen. I realized that I was standing a little too close for someone who I had just met, so I turned to take a few meaningful steps away from him, and, because my back was to him, he took advantage of the situation and slapped my butt just as my roommate walked in. Perfect.

After that, we went back into the other room and tried to watch Fight Club, except that Robin kept wanting to show us various music videos. When his incessant chatter subsided, his hand reached up to take the place of his voice, ambling slowly around my body, beginning with my other leg — you know, the one that Blake wasn’t already touching. The presence of a blanket that had been in that room to begin with created a helpful? barrier to prevent either of the two men becoming aware of their parallel movements, nor did it allow Sarah, the girl who Robin had just made up with and apparently decided to be in a relationship with, to know that her current boyfriend currently had his hand on my leg. touching another girl.

As I debated whether it was better to call him out and risk her getting upset and leaving, or just ignore it and hope for the best,

I brought Robin and Sarah over and gave them some relationship counseling while they lay on the couch and I sat on the rolling chair. Sarah explained all about her relationship and how it had been happening – that Robin had broken up with her because she started dating other people, and that she had eventually changed her mind and thought she could be with just one person and decided that Robin was the person and then that Robin had done something slightly mean to her right when she’d decided that…they’d gone on another date the night before, in which they’d climbed a mountain and sat at the top and discussed their relationship.

I asked Robin if he understood what Sarah was saying about her change of mind about monogamy. Sarah thanked me for bringing that to his attention and they continued with their argument.

As we watched the movie, Robin’s hand began to trace a pattern down my shin, ever so gently. In the same time, Blake had his arm around my shoulders and was playing around with my collar bone. Robin’s hand was under the blanket and so Sarah was ostensibly in the dark about his actions while he also was cuddling with her on the other side of himself.

We went into the kitchen and he pulled me into a hug. My roommate came into the room and I pulled away from the hug because I didn’t want to appear too cuddly but my date took the opportunity of me walking away to give me a pat on the butt.

I received another text from cat boy asking if I was good at British Humor and I didn’t respond. After the movie I received a call from Mr. Cat Boy telling me that he had left his uncle’s house to retrieve his cat from his own house and was now on his way back to his uncle’s house, cat in car. I asked Blake and Robin and Sarah if they were interested in Cat Boy’s hot tub and they all seemed excited so I asked Cat Boy if I could bring a bunch of friends over that I was hanging out with to his hot tub and if he’d like to come and finish watching the movie with us and all drive there together or whatever.

Cat Boy called me when he arrived and my roommate let him in. He appeared in our sitting area and I jumped up from my place inside Blake’s arm and under Robin’s finger. He took a seat on our yoga ball and I sat down on our rolling chair next to his yoga ball. It was now an extremely tense silence as we watched the movie. Blake, from what I could see of him without turning my head to look at him, appeared flabberghasted that I now had another date besides him to sit next to and the blanket remained away from their legs, neither Blake nor Robin bothered to replace it.

The silence got to be too much and Cat Boy leapt up and told me that he was going to go get his cat from the car where he apparently had been waiting for the return of his lover. I went with him to his car, leaving the awkward scene that I’d been smoldering under for the past hour and a half or so. We walked outside into the bristling dark, neither of us saying much. When we got to his car, he said in a sort of scared and cutting voice “Is that your date?” I said that it wasn’t my particular date, no, that I had only met him that day on Tinder and that Cat Boy was also my date, or that I didn’t need to have a particular date, it was at times possible for one to have multiple dates in the same evening and even at the same time. Somehow, astonishingly, this seemed to make Cat Boy feel better. He collected Kitty from the back seat and we stood in front of his car. I asked him what he thought we were and whether he was planning on leaving and he said he didn’t think we were anything, or that we were casually dating or whatever and that he was planning on leaving unless I — and then he stopped and didn’t finish his sentence and I asked him and he said unless I told the other guy that he was my date and finished with a nevermind. I didn’t answer him. It was really dark and weird outside and we were lingering in front of his car. I wanted to touch him, to hug him or more immediately to kiss him but his hands were in front of his chest and I felt that he might have felt invaded by such actions. It had been raining that day and the street was especially black with rain water.

As I pondered this conundrum, Kitty chose this moment to leap out of Cat Boy’s hands and ran off into the parking lot of the house next door to mine. Cat Boy looked at me with alarm and we both followed in the direction he’d run off to. I was under the impression that since Cat Boy and Kitty spent so much time together that he didn’t have any difficulty with getting kitty to come to him if he so wanted. Cat Boy called for kitty and looked increasingly alarmed as we searched for kitty underneath some plants that we’d seen him crawl into, and then to the other side of the parking lot underneath a car.

It was at this point that we heard a strange sound that seemed to be coming out of the place where Kitty was hiding. Though it might have been a cat, it sounded like an alien speaking in its own alien language, giving a speech to its brethren of aliens before they returned to their mission. Cat Boy and I looked at each other and agreed that it was the strangest sound either of us had ever experienced. Could it possibly be coming from his very own Kitty?

It was at this time that Blake and Robin came strolling down the sidewalk, suddenly fast friends due to their common interest: marijuana. Cat Boy got a can from his car and opened it with a can opener and set it down by our feet, and kitty came and found the food and started to eat some of it. I asked Cat Boy if he would still watch the movie with us and he said that he needed to get Kitty home.

I walked him back to his car which was silver and mentioned that I’d like to see him in the future.

I went back inside and while I’d been gone, it seemed that Blake and Christopher Robin had transitioned from blindly competing for my affection, to the role of dealer. We returned to our former formation and I replaced the blanket over all three of us while Sarah and Blake continued their awkward tense romantic encounter.

We finished Monty Python and the Holy Grail with little talking, and Sarah and Robin left. Blake, however, stayed, and we ended up sleeping on the couch together.

In the morning, however, I woke up in my bed, to Blake anxiously tugging the covers back, and saying that we needed to do something. It took longer than you might expect for me to actually leave my bed, probably because I didn’t want to. He mentioned Voodoo Doughnuts and several other touristy destination and was aghast, insisting it would be blasphemous to live in Portland without having visited. I couldn’t say no, such were the rules of the game. We drove in his beat up car that was parked down the street, to Downtown Portland.

It had rained the night before, and when I unexpectedly tripped on a crack in the sidewalk, Blake surprised me by chiding himself, muttering that he should have been taking better care, and grabbed my wrist so as to make sure I didn’t hurt myself again. To this day I can’t help but find it funny that he considered himself responsible for my own clumsiness.

He bought me a doughnut in the shape of a voodoo doll. It came with a pretzel stick, and you could poke it to release the strawberry or raspberry jam. Next we went into a restaurant that was supposed to have an amazing view of the city, though it was mostly parking lots that we could see from this window. Nevertheless, Blake explained the significance of each one, telling me he’d once danced as a male stripper in that one over there, he’d once parked his car in another and it had almost gotten towed.

The patrons of the restaurant, seated and enjoying what appeared to be an expensive meal, were flummoxed by the presence of two people, simply staring out the window, and eventually we left. I deduced that perhaps his insistence had something to do with going to his parents house, which he next took me to. On the way, he explained the situation — that they had kicked him out after his dad had gotten remarried. Once occupying the basement, his dad and his new step mom had now filled it with all sorts of non-essential objects — an old yoga ball, exercise equipment etc. In fact it was stacked to the brim with an assortment of boxes that held all sorts of things poking out.

When we got there, he snuck in through the bottom window, and then, presumably raced upstairs and opened the large double doors where I was waiting, as instructed. He took a shower and gave me his phone so I could read through all his old tinder messages. I started to feel sick as I saw how persistent he was with other girls, reading between their silences that they were no longer interested. Blake was an avid texter, it seemed, using hoards of nonsensical emojis to convey even the simplest point.

and Blake stayed and we had sex and he slept over and we hung out the entire next day including going to voodoo doughnuts, a place we could see the city out the window of a building, and his parents house who apparently desparately wanted him to leave. I read all of his previous tinder messages on his phone and they were weird and unfortunately he obviously spewed way too much random information on his dates so that it seemed unlikely that any of them would remain interested for that long. We hooked up again, we talked about sex toys, he told me more about his ex girlfriend who was a stripper. He gave me head for the third time and we talked about his mom and the potential of her coming downstairs and how particularly bad their marriage was. He took a shower and asked me to get something for him which I did obediently but didn’t get in the shower with him and I don’t know if that’s why he asked me to come in there in the first place, it could have been just so that he could have the razor that was on the floor next to the shower. I continued reading his tinder messages with different girls and one old woman who had sent him a few pictures of her genitalia. We laid in bed for a while and we talked about what we were each looking for or no he asked me what my plan was for the next five years after asking me what my deepest darkest secret was to which I replied that I had the weirdest decision making technique. He said he would like to meet a girl who he could spend a significant amount of time with and be in a relationship with and that he sort of missed his ex girlfriend who was a stripper and that his friends and parents told him that he could do better, and that her friends said the same thing about him and that eventually they’d broken up for whatever reason.

On

I was anxious to get home, as an old friend was coming to stay with me that night. As we drove back through the night, I found myself engrossed, or at least tolerating, a story about

Blake had an increasingly annoying habit of jabbering nonstop about anything and everything and my hints that I would like him to stop talking got more and more direct until I’d done something new and told him point blank that he needed to stop talking. Confused, he complied, and I enjoyed the awkward silence that ensued like no other.

When we arrived, he asked if he could come inside to use my bathroom and get a drink of water, and then somehow, amazingly, roped me into giving him a haircut. He insisted on himself cleaning the tufts of hair now littering the bathroom floor, and I produced a small electric vacuum as requested.

Time inched forward; he still had not gone, and eventually it was too late and my friends had arrived.

I stalled by going to meet them outside, hoping he’d somehow, miraculously have disappeared by the time I got back. No such luck. He was waiting for us back in the kitchen. Not only that, but insisted on making small talk as my friend stood against the oven, and he leaned against the sink in our small kitchen.

❦

Your notes on Robin, Blake, David & Sarah

no. 18 · someone i met once

Charlie & George

After midnight, a new-looking Prius.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

It was already after midnight when my best male friend from college, and his roommate pulled up in a new looking prius. I was nervous, had anxiously anticipated their arrival; they were passing through on a road trip and I literally jumped into my friend’s arms to keep the score even, he passed me to George, who seemed to have slight difficulty supporting my weight.

I stalled inviting them inside, hoping I would see my previous guest slip out the front door, but no such luck. We arrived to find him still standing in the kitchen and I muttered some explanation. Charlie, always infinitely polite, made conversation, and then told me he seemed nice. After this, I guided them towards my favorite all night coffee house.

My luck was testing me for who should we meet, lingering in the doorway, blocking our entrance, but Jake. Jake whose bed I’d shared only a week earlier. He was wearing an all white jumpsuit and brandishing a power drill menacingly, and told Charlie that he’d been stealing construction tools like drills from somewhere nearby..

I pretended I’d never met him before. We went inside and played a game with frogs and I paid for Charlie’s drink. I got a mango smoothie. then we went to Matthew’s house and sat on the couch for a bit until he came up and told us to get the fuck out with a bare chest and then we walked around outside and talked about tinder and George said the best line for his profile was “kill me” after trying a number of them and Charlie talked about the short person complex.

We arranged where to sleep and Charlie asked me if we could all sleep in the same bed — I offered them all the options — that they could sleep on the couch in the living room, or in my bed with me and they chose bed and Charlie wanted to know if he could sleep with his head next to me instead of his feet (?) and I said yes.

Then we all changed into our pajamas and played a game where we had to list experiences falling under a particular category to each other. Then we went to sleep and first he had his back to me and then he did not and then in the middle of the night when we were both sleeping we, and it was very hot, seemed to put our legs together.

Who cares what happened the next day — it doesn’t matter. Charlie and George came and visited me and we did a lot of things. We went to the Gorge on one day and we got doughnuts on the next day and we did a lot of things beside this. We went to the holocaust museum.

I wasn’t sure how to feel I was a terrible tour guide, having only seen the insides of my date’s houses. having not visited many places since I’d been there, We visited the rose garden Charlie and I play fought on the stage, becoming more and more physically aggressive until he eventually picked me up and I screamed and laughed to put me down.

On the one hand, it seemed a tad trite to experience sadness, at this, a place that was created to foster grief. Yet the moment was so truly mine that I adopted a somber expression, and they, I think, wished they were somewhere, anywhere else. We went downtown and watched a skyscraper being built, discussing what it would be like to live in the elevator built to carry wood between floor and ceiling.

As we walked, Charlie brushed into me, I nudged him back. We didn’t acknowledge this was happening but kept the conversation with George going. I fell into him again, the physical contact seeming progressively more intentional. It wasn’t acknowledged. On the day before they left, they dropped me off in their car at the Vision Action Group, which I must have described as boring, because, though I begged them to come inside and stay for a while, they told me they must be on their way.

They were headed to their next destination and hit me up on the way back.

no. 19 · someone i met once

Ryan

Tea from a green teapot with a silver lid.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

I watched him drink tea out of a green tea pot with a silver lid. He had a laptop that was in a briefcase and papers in piles on the table in front of him. I had just come from the supermarket and was carrying two heavy bags of groceries, which I was struggling with.

I went to rest at a table in front of the southeast grind and made myself a little bowl of cereal with one of their water cups and a spoon to mix the almond milk in. When I glanced back inside, I accidentally made eye contact with a cute red haired boy around my age and then looked away again.

In order to mix the milk into the cereal I’d bought, I would need a vessel. I grabbed one of the plastic cups for water and again accidentally made eye contact. When I went inside I saw a red-haired boy sitting at a table by himself. He had a laptop and a brief case and a mess of papers set out in front of him.

He had a green teapot on the table. I always wondered who drank tea at this place when it was about \$6 for a cup and all it included was hot water and a tea bag. I left my groceries outside as I could see them from the window, and slumped down onto the couch, every now and then staring at the boy with the red hair without either of us saying anything.

His head was behind the tea pot but I could still see his eyes. It seemed he was intermittently stopping what he was doing just to stare at me. Eventually I got up to go home but came back in to put the cup and spoon away I’d used to eat my cereal. It was then that he approached me and said he had to at least talk to the person he’d been staring at for the past hour or so.

Yes! Success. He helped me carry my groceries back to my house and hung around in my room a little while I put them away. He told me he was on his way to two parties and though I’d decided somewhere around that time that he wasn’t quite as interesting as his blue eyes had at first suggested, I agreed to accompany him on his evening out, interested in a change of scenery.

We walked back to the grind together where it was revealed that unlike me who got everywhere on foot, he actually had a car. It wasn’t a great car — it was old and kind of small and probably a whitish brown color. The backseat, like his table, was piled high with paperwork. On the way we chatted about this and that — what I did for a living and what he did.

The first party was at a beautiful house where everyone was quite friendly. Everyone assumed I was his girlfriend and we had a strange time explaining that we’d met just an hour earlier at a coffee shop. Ryan went off to sit on the counter in the kitchen and drink beer with his friend who he had not seen in a long time and I joined the rest of the party where they were in the middle of explaining a strange game which involved many different-colored plastic pyramids which could be stacked on top of each other to win the game.

Although it looked fun, the rules were inexcusably complex and the objective seemed like an afterthought. More and more people were joining our table and needed the rules to be explained again and again. It emerged that one small gray triangle was missing, and that we had gotten most of the rules wrong. Claire, thin and waifish who was steering the game had a special smile as if to say “we would never play monopoly.” and her partner Brandon, seemed used to following her lead, and only a bit like there was something wrong with his brain that his attractiveness was making up for.

He had a crew cut to match his sad blue eyes. Claire and I were similarly enthusiastic about anything and everything — whether it made sense to be or not. Ryan and I had to go — there was another party his main best friend’s birthday at a restaurant in downtown — but not before I mentioned to Claire that I was looking for a job and Claire told me to apply at a summer camp for especially intelligent children who wanted to use their summer to sew and to program computers.

I jotted down my contact details and we left to drive 15 miles across town; all the while he was explaining his weed business to me. I think I somehow managed to give him the impression that I was both impressed and interested so that’s what we talked about when we stopped at lights. It was very dark and there were lots of winding roads.

I couldn’t be sure I’d ever been to this part of Portland even during the day. After he had built up the party so much, saying how it was his very best friend so he couldn’t miss it, no one was really paying any attention to us. we were sitting on the end away from his friend.

We were playing Never Have I Ever which someone had apparently taken the time to make into an actual board game version with cards and stuff. Except no one seemed to have done anything that the cards said and everyone had these nervous smiles like they were trying not to let anyone into their thoughts.

We agreed that we were both hungry and decided to leave and get crepes. We walked to a crepe place and talked about the part of town we were in. We ordered a banana Nutella crepe to share and discussed what it meant to date and variations to the norm concept like dating multiple people or dating people of the same gender.

He addressed the topic as though I might not have considered it before, strangely, and seemed to be informing me of alternatives to a way of thinking I had not expressed explicitly. I suppose he lumped me in with mainstream opinions. It reminded me a little of how my first boyfriend liked to tell me about things he knew and thought I didn’t.

When the check came (about \$7.50 for the crepe we’d shared), he eyed me mischievously, and asked me conspiratorially if I wanted to put what I had just learned from him to the test. So we split the check. Then we drove to his house, which seemed a bit on the outskirts of town. Instead of a mattress, he simply had lots of pillows and blankets bunched together on the floor (he said he’d just moved in).

My eyes glanced around his room; there was a bookshelf with many unknown treasures. The floor was pleasant hardwood, and seemed clean (he had just moved in). Then we went into the kitchen and he stood in front of the cabinet while I sat on the counter while we talked about the different kinds of tea he had and I told him I didn’t really like tea.

He got two mugs and boiled water and put the bags in those little metal steeping ball things. I think I picked chamomile. We laid on the couch together for a while with his head on my lap (he asked if it was ok to put it there) and then went into his room and he told me I could pick out a big shirt from his closet to wear to bed and made a point of closing his eyes while I changed in the space between his closet and his “bed” which was just a pile of blankets on the floor.

His room was sparse and it had lots of CDs and small things on the wall. He had a bit of weed paraphernalia on it too, and a tan bookshelf with a lot of books in it. We told each other stories as we were falling asleep and in the morning he woke up early and left the room and then he came back so we could cuddle.

In the morning, he asked if I wanted to come grocery shopping with him and he drove us even farther out of town, to a Korean Grocery Store he apparently frequented, and he bought things that I’d never heard of — various kinds of noodles, and seaweed, and I looked for those jelly cup things my mom used to buy my brother and I, hoping to reminisce about how we’d smush them out into our mouths as young children.

Then he drove me back to the place we’d started — my little blue house where my two roommates were chatting amiably on the couch. Though we’d now spent almost 24 hours together, I invited him inside. He said he hadn’t considered coming inside but that now he was here he might as well. My roommates were both there when we got in and I sat at the chair at the table while he sat on the couch and my roommate lay at the other end.

We told them what we had done on our date. It turned out he had helped my roommate book a show a long time ago. He returned a minute after he left because he’d forgotten to get my number and kissed me (for the first time) on the lips behind the curtain that closed off the kitchen so my roommates didn’t see.

After he left, both of my roommates told me that they liked him and that I should invest in him. They said he was attractive. Alpha said that we seemed to have some chemistry. Later that week, Greg told me I should stop going on dates with other people and just try to go out with him again.

I didn’t have my phone so I couldn’t text him until Thursday when I went to retrieve it from David’s house and then I texted him excitedly except he only replied in one word answers so I gave up. I called him when I decided to take the job I’d been offered at the party he took me to and he called me back about a week later but didn’t return my call after that.

I ran into him a long time after that when I was walking towards a library with Westley and he walked in the opposite direction as soon as I saw him but when I made eye contact and casually said hi to him he said hi back.

I watched him drink tea out of a green tea pot with a silver lid. He had a laptop that was in a briefcase and papers in piles on the table in front of him.

I had just come from the supermarket and was carrying two heavy bags of groceries, which I was struggling with. I went to rest at a table in front of the southeast grind and made myself a little bowl of cereal with one of their water cups and a spoon to mix the almond milk in. When I glanced back inside, I accidentally made eye contact with a cute red haired boy around my age and then looked away again.

In order to mix the milk into the cereal I’d bought, I would need a vessel. I grabbed one of the plastic cups for water and again accidentally made eye contact. When I went inside I saw a red-haired boy sitting at a table by himself. He had a laptop and a brief case and a mess of papers set out in front of him. He had a green teapot on the table. I always wondered who drank tea at this place when it was about \$6 for a cup and all it included was hot water and a tea bag.

I left my groceries outside as I could see them from the window, and slumped down onto the couch, every now and then staring at the boy with the red hair without either of us saying anything. His head was behind the tea pot but I could still see his eyes. It seemed he was intermittently stopping what he was doing just to stare at me.

Eventually I got up to go home but came back in to put the cup and spoon away I’d used to eat my cereal. It was then that he approached me and said he had to at least talk to the person he’d been staring at for the past hour or so. Yes! Success. He helped me carry my groceries back to my house and hung around in my room a little while I put them away. He told me he was on his way to two parties and though I’d decided somewhere around that time that he wasn’t quite as interesting as his blue eyes had at first suggested, I agreed to accompany him on his evening out, interested in a change of scenery.

We walked back to the grind together where it was revealed that unlike me who got everywhere on foot, he actually had a car. It wasn’t a great car — it was old and kind of small and probably a whitish brown color. The backseat, like his table, was piled high with paperwork. On the way we chatted about this and that — what I did for a living and what he did.

The first party was at a beautiful house where everyone was quite friendly. Everyone assumed I was his girlfriend and we had a strange time explaining that we’d met just an hour earlier at a coffee shop.

Ryan went off to sit on the counter in the kitchen and drink beer with his friend who he had not seen in a long time and I joined the rest of the party where they were in the middle of explaining a strange game which involved many different-colored plastic pyramids which could be stacked on top of each other to win the game. Although it looked fun, the rules were inexcusably complex and the objective seemed like an afterthought.

More and more people were joining our table and needed the rules to be explained again and again. It emerged that one small gray triangle was missing, and that we had gotten most of the rules wrong. Claire, thin and waifish who was steering the game had a special smile as if to say “we would never play monopoly.” and her partner Brandon, seemed used to following her lead, and only a bit like there was something wrong with his brain that his attractiveness was making up for. He had a crew cut to match his sad blue eyes.

Claire and I were similarly enthusiastic about anything and everything — whether it made sense to be or not. Ryan and I had to go — there was another party his main best friend’s birthday at a restaurant in downtown — but not before I mentioned to Claire that I was looking for a job and Claire told me to apply at a summer camp for especially intelligent children who wanted to use their summer to sew and to program computers. I jotted down my contact details and we left to drive 15 miles across town; all the while he was explaining his weed business to me. I think I somehow managed to give him the impression that I was both impressed and interested so that’s what we talked about when we stopped at lights. It was very dark and there were lots of winding roads. I couldn’t be sure I’d ever been to this part of Portland even during the day.

After he had built up the party so much, saying how it was his very best friend so he couldn’t miss it, no one was really paying any attention to us. we were sitting on the end away from his friend.

We were playing Never Have I Ever which someone had apparently taken the time to make into an actual board game version with cards and stuff. Except no one seemed to have done anything that the cards said and everyone had these nervous smiles like they were trying not to let anyone into their thoughts.

We agreed that we were both hungry and decided to leave and get crepes. We walked to a crepe place and talked about the part of town we were in. We ordered a banana Nutella crepe to share and discussed what it meant to date and variations to the norm concept like dating multiple people or dating people of the same gender. He addressed the topic as though I might not have considered it before, strangely, and seemed to be informing me of alternatives to a way of thinking I had not expressed explicitly. I suppose he lumped me in with mainstream opinions. It reminded me a little of how my first boyfriend liked to tell me about things he knew and thought I didn’t.

When the check came (about \$7.50 for the crepe we’d shared), he eyed me mischievously, and asked me conspiratorially if I wanted to put what I had just learned from him to the test. So we split the check.

Then we drove to his house, which seemed a bit on the outskirts of town. Instead of a mattress, he simply had lots of pillows and blankets bunched together on the floor (he said he’d just moved in). My eyes glanced around his room; there was a bookshelf with many unknown treasures. The floor was pleasant hardwood, and seemed clean (he had just moved in).

Then we went into the kitchen and he stood in front of the cabinet while I sat on the counter while we talked about the different kinds of tea he had and I told him I didn’t really like tea. He got two mugs and boiled water and put the bags in those little metal steeping ball things. I think I picked chamomile.

We laid on the couch together for a while with his head on my lap (he asked if it was ok to put it there) and then went into his room and he told me I could pick out a big shirt from his closet to wear to bed and made a point of closing his eyes while I changed in the space between his closet and his “bed” which was just a pile of blankets on the floor. His room was sparse and it had lots of CDs and small things on the wall. He had a bit of weed paraphernalia on it too, and a tan bookshelf with a lot of books in it. We told each other stories as we were falling asleep and in the morning he woke up early and left the room and then he came back so we could cuddle.

In the morning, he asked if I wanted to come grocery shopping with him and he drove us even farther out of town, to a Korean Grocery Store he apparently frequented, and he bought things that I’d never heard of — various kinds of noodles, and seaweed, and I looked for those jelly cup things my mom used to buy my brother and I, hoping to reminisce about how we’d smush them out into our mouths as young children.

Then he drove me back to the place we’d started — my little blue house where my two roommates were chatting amiably on the couch. Though we’d now spent almost 24 hours together, I invited him inside.

He said he hadn’t considered coming inside but that now he was here he might as well. My roommates were both there when we got in and I sat at the chair at the table while he sat on the couch and my roommate lay at the other end. We told them what we had done on our date. It turned out he had helped my roommate book a show a long time ago.

He returned a minute after he left because he’d forgotten to get my number and kissed me (for the first time) on the lips behind the curtain that closed off the kitchen so my roommates didn’t see.

After he left, both of my roommates told me that they liked him and that I should invest in him. They said he was attractive. Alpha said that we seemed to have some chemistry. Later that week, Greg told me I should stop going on dates with other people and just try to go out with him again.

I didn’t have my phone so I couldn’t text him until Thursday when I went to retrieve it from David’s house and then I texted him excitedly except he only replied in one word answers so I gave up. I called him when I decided to take the job I’d been offered at the party he took me to and he called me back about a week later but didn’t return my call after that. I ran into him a long time after that when I was walking towards a library with Westley and he walked in the opposite direction as soon as I saw him but when I made eye contact and casually said hi to him he said hi back.

We met at the hilt where I’d chosen because it was close to Feather and Joey’s house where I was at their vision action group previously. When I got there he presented me with a gift — a thing he’d made which was a few drawings inside of one of those pamphlets you get in airplanes that tell you about all of the safety features and what to do in the event of an emergency.

He told me about a doll he had at his house which he and his roommates took turns hiding from each other, and then about a movie he had made. He paid for my drink (we had one beer each) and we also talked about what it was like to move to a new city and not necessarily have a lot of friends.

He said that he lived in a house with people he knew from before Portland that was pretty out of the way and for that reason he didn’t necessarily have a lot of friends out of his particular housing situation. He said he was going to have a party in a few months and I asked if he could invite me and he said that he would.

As we left, I asked if he would be willing to film future dates for me and he agreed reluctantly, stating that it would be hard for him, considering he had already garnered some feelings in the short time we’d been together and would be jealous. I hadn’t considered that and dismissed him from the task.

We discussed, on the walk away from Alberta, his previous relationship and why it had ended which was not for any unamicable reasons but had simply grown apart and he felt he didn’t want to take care of her anymore. a lot of times on okcupid dates people had to explain, in very nice terms, why they had broken up with their previous boyfriends.

no. 24 · someone i met once

Kyle II

From Kyle’s perspective.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

(from kyle’s perspective): I think you’ll appreciate the irony of the situation. So I took someone’s advice and have been trying internet dating and it is something. I can’t quite rank up the strangeness of the dates I’ve been on but this might be #1 out of a small number, yet. But I already know I’m a strange attractor.

I’m unsure of the ratio on the site but the men vastly outnumber the ladies, I’m fairly certain. So it came to my surprise when a woman messaged me saying I looked interesting but how could she be certain? So I assured her I was who I am and exchanged some messages — soon enough I asked her if she would go out for coffee with me and she replied yes: either sometime later in the year or at 4 AM next week.

Pfft. All I could think was why not? I wasn’t all that worried about having my organs harvested and where do you get coffee at 4 AM anyway? So I asked where and there is a place, yay verily, there is a place. So fast forwards to the day or late night we finally set upon and eventually the texts start volleying around 1 AM when I learn she’s at a bar and needs a ride.

So with a hop-skip and a-do I arrive to meet her. She’s at least sober which was different than another person/place but she told me she had been up for over 24 hours, which as I was already asking — tweaker? Poker face already engaged we had a nice chat at the bar for awhile, her asking about my life, what I do, how’s my luck with dating online, pleasant stuff and we shared a few things in common.

She did seem quite out of it, bobbing her head to the music, scribbling on a napkin, asking pretty personal questions, but fine, I just wanted to get to know someone, and that’s what I was doing. I didn’t want to drink all night and neither did she so we decided to go to the 24 hour coffee place she likes.

That’s where things get strange. Soon as we mosey up to order coffee one of her old daters was already there to greet us. A regular 2 AM coffee addict no doubt. She told me he was a past date and they talk before ordering and me and him just exchange funny glances. A couple more awkward moments later I have my cup of java and we go to sit down.

The past dater joins us for a bit but he got tired of standing and listening to my tired mind babbling for my date. A victory I’d take but it wouldn’t last. My babbling continues and I at least have her laughing — at me or with me it didn’t matter. Either way I had an attractive audience and things don’t matter at 2 in the morning after being up all day prior.

She’s a master of Socratic dialogue. She would pretend to know less than she let on and smirk at my mansplaining. She would ask questions of some of the stupid things I said and trip me up. But she made it clear she liked me. She asked if I knew where to get cocaine. “No” was my hasty reply.

“No”. I told her I tried it but not how dumb I consider it. All of a sudden look. Here’s a guy walking in she went on two dates with. O.O. Poker face. Emptiness of thought and mind. I’ve prepared for stupid stuff like this dammit. Sometime later in our conversation I told her how nice it is to suffer from depersonalization at times.

She gets a call. A guy she dated last week wants to meet her and he’s already on his way. Fine I tell her. Fine I don’t care. She tells me she wants to get six of the smartest men she meets online and take them on a bus out into the wilderness where they will learn how to be better people.

What’s this called I ask? “Imagination Land” she tells me. Is there a walled compound involved? No, there’s a castle. I think I must have slipped into that special 3 AM place which madmen witness on occasion. I felt alarmingly at home there. Her other date cruises up on his long board and we go outside to meet him and his nice dog Hero.

Hero was probably the greatest thing of that night. I’ve always liked dogs. Anyway we shake hands and make introductions. I share his joint and fight rising nausea. He tells me he’s on acid, works at a marijuana dispensary, and studies English in college and then starts singing in German. I am an outside observer to the situation I find myself in I tell myself.

And to make this long story shorter we four including Hero went back to her place and hung out on her bed where she invited us to live with her for the next two days and dress us up in her cloths. I hugged and said my goodbyes not too long after. Haven’t seen her since.

no. 25 · someone i met once

Devin

I came to his party with another date.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

He invited me to a party at his house after we both flaked on dinner at a Mexican restaurant and I responded a week later (the day of the party) that I was on my way and bringing another date. The address he’d given me I realized once I started walking was devoid of a street — in fact, it was only numbers.

So I called him to confirm, my other date waiting politely on the grass where we were resting. He sounded surprisingly chill: not nervous and like he was having a pretty good time. The second thing he said on the phone was that he’d just made a cup of mushroom tea and was about to drink it.

After a thorough sun burning and me promising catboy that you could bring a date to another date if the other date was actually a party (“parties have lots of people”) we arrived at his house to three or so girls lounging on their “slip n’ slide” (was like three feet long, definitely for babies) in almost no clothing.

My date was not in sight and nobody knew who the fuck me and my other date were. We went through the driveway to the side yard. Ironically, the party was like a middle school party in that the boys were playing beer pong and the girls were on the slip n’ slide and they were apparently not drunk enough to interact.

The first thing that happened to me, even before I met the person I was supposed to meet, was this one boy who I would call a basic boy, asked me how old I was. I replied 22 and he acted very suspicious. He then said he could see my nipples and reached out and grabbed one.

I was in a good mood cause of the sun so my admonishment was not nearly enough to teach him a lesson. (Later he told me and his roommate that he’d slept with over 200 girls and we speculated how the nipple grabbing might have evolved into intercourse so many times). My date came out of the house.

He was extremely skinny and had messy platinum blonde hair. He was shirtless, wearing a black bathing suit. He was very white and you could see his nipples too. We sat down to talk with my other date at the head of the table and he and I across from each other. When I say sat down to talk, I mean that a time lapse of the scene might have caught him sitting across from me a few times.

He got up every three minutes to meander into the yard. The conversation came to me getting kicked out of school and he and his roommate got excited and gathered to hear the answer. When I told them, they both seemed nonplussed. “That’s it?” said my date and the other boy wandered away. “I was expecting something crazy.”

Catboy made very little conversation while I talked to mushroom boy and I helped myself to a solo cup half filled with vodka. I led him by the hand to the swing set and tried to make out with him. Pavel

The waiters thought I’d been stood up.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

After about five minutes, he still hadn’t arrived and I began picking up and putting down my coffee (because it was too hot) and pretending I couldn’t tell that all the waiters who passed by me each like five times felt bad because they thought I’d been stood up. He texted me that he was there but was too shy to actually come inside…so I went outside to meet him.

He hated the breakfast place or it was way too fancy. He by the way was very skinny, with shiny brown hair running down his back, had a pretty face, and was wearing all black. We moved outside. We shared a mushroom and goat cheese omelette which was delicious but less delicious than the beautiful day we were seeing walk by us.

He told me a story about his ex-girlfriend, who had been into Bondage. Upon her request, he had done things like slap her, and spit in her mouth, but did not like doing these things, and I could see the discomfort stretch across his face as he discussed this with me. We tried to split it evenly, but he paid because I realized I didn’t have enough.

After that we walked amiably to my house, except that he didn’t talk very much and I became a nervous Nancy, beginning thoughts and then deeming them not interesting enough to continue. We weren’t even walking at the same pace. On the way we picked up a tiny dictionary from a garage sale, and We arrived at my house and where I stayed in bed after he left, basically starving.

When we got there, we settled into my bed which was, really, the only place to hang out in my room, and looked through men I’d been messaging with on tinder. He started messaging one of them nonsense about muscle milk and rather than actually having sex, we proceeded to sort of moan and make sex noises, bashing each other lightly in the chest.

Eventually he left as the sun was going down and I crawled back into my bed, knowing there was nothing to eat in the house except some stale cereal, and feeling empty, drained, and to be honest, a bit depressed. Perhaps it was the hangover finally catching up with me, (though I didn’t feel sick or have a headache), but more likely it was the way the darkness had slowly crawled in through the windows, interrupting my peaceful day, and reminding me that, despite having seen so very many people that day and the previous, I was still, now, very much alone.

Despite my better judgment, I returned once again, to the only friend I really had, OkCupid itself, and messaged someone, convincing them to meet me even at this late hour, with the promise that they could sleep over if they couldn’t find transportation home this late at night. My last resort was his kismet, as he explained he hadn’t checked his okcupid in over a month and had somehow opened it to find my message immediately.

Michael Mount

Mostly I remember the bus.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

What I most remember from this date is being on the bus. It was a long bus trip and I had to make a transfer at night in a place I’d never been before. Usually I don’t mind being out at night alone but something about waiting for a bus is the most maddening thing.

Because it doesn’t come, and you’ve just been sitting there that whole time, who’s to say you’re not crazy for imagining you could predict when a 20 ton vehicle would swoop you up out of the blue in the middle of the night and take you precisely where you wanted to go. My brother had set up a play date with a guy he knew from college.

I couldn’t quite believe that someone so incredibly good looking would want to be my brother’s friend, who I knew as nerdy As it turned out, we had another date joining us that night, and he made it clear that ours was the date and not Michael’s as he quickly slipped the bartender a \$20 and said he was paying for my drink too.

It was our little secret, though surely Jon would’ve mentioned we’d come here together before. We brought the beers..I imagined for a second that I didn’t know him previously, that we’d just happened to meet, and because we’d gone to the bar together, and he liked me, he’d decided to pay for my drink. We didn’t discuss our previous meetings but he slipped me a quick smile at the same time as he slipped the bartender the bill.

I don’t quite remember what we talked about on the date. I know we played a game called cuthroat which is meant for three people but to be honest, is the clumsiest game I could imagine. I wasn’t really in the running but I would clumsily take my shots anyway, preparing the motion of my hands like a ritual and wondering what it was they could value so much about being able to shoot a ball into a tiny pocket.

I didn’t understand it. On the sidelines, I talked to Michael about his book, which was an expose on a fictional narcissist. I was surprised that he’d written a whole book, and that he was talking about it so nonchalantly. Afterwards I went home with Jon Storch and didn’t see Michael Mount again. Jon and I didn’t have sex that night, instead I told him awkwardly that I thought we were better off as friends, assuming he would agree as he hand’t indicated he’d like to date me.

Thereafter we settled into an uncomfortable silence which ended with us spooning our way to sleep. In fact, Jon had mentioned his frequent tuesday night games with the legendary michael on our first date, which happened to be at the exact place he’d suggested. I played along, texting both people who evidently hadn’t discussed that Jon already knew me.

no. 29 · someone i met once

Xander

He mansplained me feminism.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

He mansplained me feminism It was late when I set this date with a delivery man and I was video chatting with my mother on the giant monitor in the living room that wasn’t mine but my roommates. My mother wanted to meet my date who arrived: tall, and in a leather jacket. There was a bar only a few blocks from my house that I rarely frequented, despite its proximity.

There was a park on the other side of it. We ordered drinks for ourselves and chose a high two person table overlooking the park. It seemed we had a lot in common as we’d both studied the same subject in college but rather than compare our experiences he used this — the fact that I was supposedly interested in the subject — as a launchpad to tell me all about his experience, including things I’d learned in my intro class.

Blech. I was bored. In spite of myself I could not figure out how a situation that had seemed so promising — he was tall, attractive and dorky to boot, we were getting beers at a bar near my house — had suddenly turned into an opportunity to explain every detail of a class trip he’d gone on with his hilarious trip leader Ralph, master of hijinx…even so I listened on, unsure how to politely steer the conversation away from this veritable hell.

Afterwards we walked around nearby. It was dark and late and a little bit spooky at night. We’d arrived at another park, or perhaps the same one from the other side when he decided to explain his policies regarding feminism. “Women are always getting hit on by guys when they don’t want to be. Honestly, I feel bad for them.

They could just be enjoying a day at the park, sitting alone reading, and suddenly there’s a swarm of guys who think it’s their personal business…” I supposed this was true but hoped to interject a bit more nuance to the situation. To be honest, this hadn’t happened to me very often, and I for one loved talking to strangers.

I felt a bit sorry that he was recounting an experience I hadn’t had for me and wished he would only give a little bit of my opinion that I might convince him this wasn’t supremely true. In a sense I felt that what he was saying was that women couldn’t quite handle themselves in public; they weren’t equipped to say no to guys that wanted their number, and he felt sorry for the poor dears who had to field off requests from men like a spartan in a cage of lions. as when I tried to speak, he sort of talked over me.

He just couldn’t seem to get past this one-sided picture of the woman minding her own business, say in the park or a public library, when suddenly, from out of nowhere, not 2 but three or four men attack her with their kind words and compliments, refusing to take no for an answer. Now I consider myself a fairly attractive girl but this has never been my experience.

Sure I’ve been asked out by the odd man or two but never a tall good looking guy like himself. In spite of himself, I felt like advising him to try just once or twice, for the sake of the women in my neighborhood, sitting alone in the park, waiting for someone too….I tried to make the point I felt like saying: “if she’s sitting in the park reading, she probably wants to be asked out.

If she didn’t want to, she could just stay home by herself.” I gave up on trying to say anything, realizing he’d literally just mansplained feminism to me After this he came home and he didn’t want to stay over. This was an undeniably strange turn of events. I couldn’t tell if he thought I didn’t want him to stay.

In any event, he put on one last youtube video which was the theme song to the show “too many cooks” which, if you haven’t seen it, goes on and on. At this point I was so done with the date that I simply told him enough was enough and that I hadn’t bargained for this hour and a half long video.

He left shortly after and we didn’t speak again.

He mansplained me feminism

It was late when I set this date with a delivery man and I was video chatting with my mother on the giant monitor in the living room that wasn’t mine but my roommates. My mother wanted to meet my date who arrived: tall, and in a leather jacket.

There was a bar only a few blocks from my house that I rarely frequented, despite its proximity. There was a park on the other side of it. We ordered drinks for ourselves and chose a high two person table overlooking the park. It seemed we had a lot in common as we’d both studied the same subject in college but rather than compare our experiences he used this — the fact that I was supposedly interested in the subject — as a launchpad to tell me all about his experience, including things I’d learned in my intro class.

Blech. I was bored. In spite of myself I could not figure out how a situation that had seemed so promising — he was tall, attractive and dorky to boot, we were getting beers at a bar near my house — had suddenly turned into an opportunity to explain every detail of a class trip he’d gone on with his hilarious trip leader Ralph, master of hijinx…even so I listened on, unsure how to politely steer the conversation away from this veritable hell.

Afterwards we walked around nearby. It was dark and late and a little bit spooky at night. We’d arrived at another park, or perhaps the same one from the other side when he decided to explain his policies regarding feminism.

“Women are always getting hit on by guys when they don’t want to be. Honestly, I feel bad for them. They could just be enjoying a day at the park, sitting alone reading, and suddenly there’s a swarm of guys who think it’s their personal business…” I supposed this was true but hoped to interject a bit more nuance to the situation.

To be honest, this hadn’t happened to me very often, and I for one loved talking to strangers. I felt a bit sorry that he was recounting an experience I hadn’t had for me and wished he would only give a little bit of my opinion that I might convince him this wasn’t supremely true. In a sense I felt that what he was saying was that women couldn’t quite handle themselves in public; they weren’t equipped to say no to guys that wanted their number, and he felt sorry for the poor dears who had to field off requests from men like a spartan in a cage of lions.

as when I tried to speak, he sort of talked over me. He just couldn’t seem to get past this one-sided picture of the woman minding her own business, say in the park or a public library, when suddenly, from out of nowhere, not 2 but three or four men attack her with their kind words and compliments, refusing to take no for an answer.

Now I consider myself a fairly attractive girl but this has never been my experience. Sure I’ve been asked out by the odd man or two but never a tall good looking guy like himself. In spite of himself, I felt like advising him to try just once or twice, for the sake of the women in my neighborhood, sitting alone in the park, waiting for someone too….I tried to make the point

I felt like saying: “if she’s sitting in the park reading, she probably wants to be asked out. If she didn’t want to, she could just stay home by herself.”

I gave up on trying to say anything, realizing he’d literally just mansplained feminism to me

After this he came home and he didn’t want to stay over. This was an undeniably strange turn of events. I couldn’t tell if he thought I didn’t want him to stay. In any event, he put on one last youtube video which was the theme song to the show “too many cooks” which, if you haven’t seen it, goes on and on. At this point I was so done with the date that I simply told him enough was enough and that I hadn’t bargained for this hour and a half long video. He left shortly after and we didn’t speak again.

no. 30 · someone i met once

Paul

After the sixth long phone call with Tyler.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

After my sixth long phone conversation with Tyler, I called one of my potential dates that I’d neglected to follow up on after they’d texted me after I’d given them my number in hopes that we could talk on the phone. He told me that he’d just gotten home from watching a movie by himself and that before that he’d gone to the park and swung on the swings by himself.

We talked about online dating and he said for him it was sad and disappointing and we agreed that meeting after messaging online took the spontaneity out of meeting potential partners. He said he’d gone one a few dates and they’d all gone horrendously bad or the people had been boring and he had or hadn’t followed up with them, that sometimes he’d followed up with them only because he wanted friends to hang out with because he was bored.

He lived with two boys – his brothers, and they were all in a band together. He’d spent the day in the recording studio. I told him that he and his brothers were probably secretly the Jonas Brothers. He said the movie he’d seen had been a chick flick but that he’d liked it a lot and that it made him feel something and that people liked movies that made them feel things.

He said that he often watched movies by himself and though it seemed like an undesirable situation, he enjoyed spending time by himself a lot. He said his brothers had moved to Portland after he’d left home and I said that he was secretly Nick Jonas from the Jonas Brothers and why hadn’t he told me that before, when we’d been talking on the dating website.

We decided to meet the next day for me to give him the art lesson. He came the next day after 4:00 and we sat down at the wooden table and I was all frantic and upset after having had nothing to eat the entire day. I was talking a lot and fast it seemed and I was trying to calm myself down but I felt I had low energy and low ability to be pleasant and calm since I was food deprived.

I had planned a lesson for him based on the book “Drawing on The right Side of the Brain” by Betty Edwards so I gave him the shell to draw and he described its surface as I asked him to do and then he took down the details on the paper. I was impressed with how much he’d captured and he said he felt that it was a very poor attempt.

I said it wasn’t fair for him to degrade his own performance like that, and that I was being genuine in saying that it was good. I was a little jealous, even, since he’d had so little training. I lectured him about observing things carefully and how you were supposed to do something and how art wasn’t about the finished product but about altering your vision.

I had him draw a gesture of me with my head on the table; the pose was inspired by feeling dead. His drawing was very good and he drew my hair and the lower half of my body and everything and it was scribbly and squiggly and once again I tried to convince him that it really was an excellent work of art.

He did a contour drawing of something else without looking. After we had done everything, he drew a maze that was born out of a drawing of my phone that I’d been holding. Then he went back and labelled all the drawings and drew himself being abducted by a flying saucer in his first shell drawing and added some flowers to the maze one and added captions and titles to all of them.

I felt like I was not standing on anything, I had no idea where to go with the art lesson, he refused to acknowledge his talent and I had not been prepared for him to already understand the basis of conceptual art and felt strange about shifting gears after I’d provided this basis of a solid foundation for our lesson based on the assumption that people were all dumb and didn’t know anything and couldn’t think for themselves.

I felt that I’d failed myself by not teaching him what he wanted to know and he seemed to be frustrated or at least tuned out of our date. I took some pictures of him with his drawings and he told me I should keep them and that I could send him pictures of them.

He said he was going to a show that was nearby and I asked if I could come if I finished my game night early and he didn’t seem especially enthusiastic about me coming but we figured out where it was together anyway on his map on his phone and he played trying to guess where the venue was (it was at a pizza place?) without typing in the address on google maps but gave up and typed it in anyway and it was where he had just gotten to with moving his finger along the roads.

I promised him I’d send him pictures of his drawings. He told me a bit about the place that he worked and I apologized for making him come all the way to my house for the short art lesson. His coworker had texted him that she had forgotten her keys and she needed to close the shop and so he had to drive back to where he worked and give her the keys.

Right before he stood up to leave, he said “Would you like to get a beer sometime?” and I couldn’t tell if his strange voice when he said that was because he was nervous about what I would say or because he didn’t necessarily actually want to or something completely different. I agreed excitedly as I hadn’t been sure that this date was going well at all, and especially not wanting to ruin my near perfect streak, and he left.

I neglected to text him the pictures and instead sent him a message saying “I never sent you the pictures” and then a wall of a few dozen emojis which he completely ignored. (We talked on the phone the night before about how he’d gone to a movie by himself and playing music in a band and he agreed to come over for an art lesson.

The next day I didn’t eat at all and then I was starving when he got there which made it hard to communicate or behave positively or concentrate on the impression I might be giving him in any regard. We sat at the table in the living room and I showed him how to do certain things with his pencil or he showed me since he was unequivocally better at drawing than me even though he’d never tried.)

Your notes on Paul

no. 31 · someone i met once

Connor

Delightfully celebratory of my drinking.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

We talked on the phone earlier that day and he appeared to be delightfully celebratory of my inclination towards becoming an alcoholic. We met up that evening, he picked me up at my house and I encouraged him to hang out in my room for a short period of time while I “got dressed.” I had procrastinated taking a shower for a while and had just put on overalls without a shirt when he called to say he’d arrived.

I went to his car, which was black and stubby, maybe a Prius or a BMW, but it was shiny. I decided not to change afterall and wore my black overalls on the date in which we went to this bar he’d told me about which was supposed to be hilarious since it had its name repeated a bunch of times.

The bar seemed like a regular old dive bar, but with straw on the floor. I don’t remember most of what we talked about but, as always, we settled on my favorite subject (online dating). He told me a little bit about some girl he’d been seeing from okcupid and how they’d ended up making out on some swings the night before and that he was gonna go on another date with her, but said that I was much more interesting and that she wasn’t very good at small talk or that they were still making small talk after going on two dates.

I told him all this other random stuff about me and my OkCupid life. He said that he doesn’t like it when girls give ultimatums on their profile like “If you’re 40, don’t even think about messaging me.” I had the idea that my profile had some things that were similar to that so I questioned him further about what he didn’t like about that.

Anyway, I bought us shots and beers I think and we drank them, and I kind of remember becoming relatively intoxicated, also the night included my going up to the bar by myself and ordering an entire plate of onion rings which I devoured singled handedly (I’m not sure I’d eaten anything that day), and which he commented that he liked how I ate them with my hands not caring etc.

I didn’t feel like he had the right to judge me for any of the things and was disappointed as on the phone he’d presented himself to me as someone who could understand my sense of humor and had a similar one, which I took to mean he might be relatively confident and unabashed at doing “weird” things, rather than the type to point them out as examples of model behavior.

He dropped me off at my house in his black car after only a few hours (it was like 11) I think he had to do something the next day, and we agreed to hang out in the future (though we didn’t).

no. 32 · someone i met once

Jasper

A friend from the Rocky Horror crowd, two a.m.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

I made a friend in the crowd that streamed out of the Rocky Horror Picture Show when it ended at the ungodly hour of two am. He led me back to one of his friend’s houses, where we proceeded to drink and talk, with the constant presence of a large gray bulldog, who probably weighed more than me and was, to be honest, making me very nervous.

The two friends I had made left abruptly and I was left in the house of this stranger, and his dog, but rather than asking me to leave, he seemed complacently friendly, perhaps happy to have the company, certainly excited to have a willing audience for his impromptu obedience class; he told me to grip the ears and if the dog didn’t listen to me, to climb on top of it and hold its ears down to show it who was boss.

I didn’t really feel like doing that right then, I wasn’t in a bossy mood, but I was intimidated by Jasper and the prospect of staying at his house even though I didn’t know him so I tried my best to follow his instructions. But I sort of just wanted to make friends with the dog and to have Jasper teach him discipline.

He was curiously invested in my progress and assumed that I was similarly invested. We went upstairs with the dog who I had begun calling “Kitty,” and I sat in his black leather chair that was directly in front of a massive stereo system as he played different records and cds. We eventually got tired and smoked weed and decided we should go to bed if we planned on getting food with his friends in the morning.

I was having all sorts of anxious but interesting thoughts, having gotten high for the first time in so long and was engrossed in them, was thinking something magical as I sat there in the black chair, was analyzing every aspect of my interaction with him, whether to make eye contact etc. Even though I was barely talking; I asked him about some of the records he’d put on, feigning a bit more knowledge of music then I really had.

He said that he worked in sound and often went record shopping and had found the records but had yet to listen to them even though he’d bought them a long time ago. We went to bed and the dog fell asleep right in between us, though we were just barely touching hands as we drifted off.

In the morning we went to a few different places, we walked around, we got coffee, we went to my house, we went to a bar that he frequents, my feet were tired from walking and my shoes were pretty uncomfortable, they were the Harley Davidson motorcycle boots and I wasn’t wearing socks. The strangest thing that happened perhaps was when we got back to my house.

Ostensibly, this would be my time to say goodbye, seeing as I had a house, and I’d been staying at his only out of convenience. Instead, this was not even mentioned. It’s unclear whether the thought of leaving me home did not occur to him; instead it remained one of many errands, no different than the rest.

It seemed I belonged with him, not in any dramatic sort of way, only in the way of camaraderie between two people who have suddenly come to share a living situation. There was no comment. The dog came with us of course and a lot of our interaction was based on talking to the dog, or him telling me about it.

I asked him questions about it. I reflected on my overwhelming desire in this situation for this interaction to be pleasant and devoid of negative feelings, which was resulting in my not talking about myself at all, not disclosing much of my personality whatsoever, and listening with feigned enthusiasm, to whatever it occurred to him to tell me.

I was also intent, perhaps, on continuing this strange encounter for as long as it might go on for. There was no end in sight. I felt any hint of my personhood might alert him to the fact that he was now harboring a second person. No, the safest way was to remain faceless, nameless, boring, uninteresting, numb.

At the bar he ordered some kind of food and I ordered a beer after a bit of deliberation and talking to the waitress about it a lot. His friends called him and said that they were nearbyish so we took the bus to the place that they were and I fell asleep in my seat for a minute.

His friends consisted of a male, about 30, who he’d known for a long time it seemed, the male’s sister, and the male’s wife. The male’s wife was wearing, I think, a very elegant sun hat and they started taking pictures in front of this guy’s jeep that had parked right in front of us except the wheels were huge so maybe it was actually a monster truck.

He and his sister swapped clothes and texted a picture of them to their mother. I couldn’t understand the relationship between the sister and the wife completely. We ordered more drinks and there was a whole thing with the bill — the wife was complaining to the waitress that she’d charged too much, the wife was supposed to foot the whole bill, I didn’t understand why, perhaps she’d been treated in the past?

The dynamics of the situation fell through the slats in my tired mind. There was a little questions about how Jasper and I knew each other and some reminiscence about how Jasper and the male knew each other. I felt like Jasper didn’t quite know how to navigate the social situation and I, for one, didn’t either.

He told a few longish stories that were met with an unenthusiastic response. We all walked back to their house and the guy barbequed some stuff in the side yard. Their apartment was very nice, everything was white, it seemed expensive. We went and sat at the picnic table in the back. The wife and sister were engrossed in a conversation and ignored me.

There was something about the food — I wasn’t hungry or it didn’t taste good. The girls were making fun of the boy for keeping on bringing out more and more food even though ostensibly no one was extremely hungry. I got in a conversation with the man and it felt a lot better than the conversations intermittently I’d been having with the two women who reminded me of everyone I’d gone to high school with.

Nevertheless, I enjoyed witnessing their burgeoning female bond and noting the things it seemed to be based on though I felt distinctly that I could not participate in it. Eventually, Jasper and I walked home and after we got home we relaxed and watched a comedy show — Sarah Silverman probably — some girl making lots of semi-funny jokes that I was engrossed in, thinking about women comics etc. and then we finally settled on watching Trainspotting which was great and I’d never seen it before.

We were cuddling on the couch and it was sweet and very cozy even though he seemed to be in a strange position. Eventually we went upstairs and went to bed and made out a little and he ran his hands over my body but didn’t take any of my clothes off. The dog came bounding onto the bed, though, and our excursion ended.

In the morning, we said goodbye on the platform between the stairs, unsure of what sort of closeness had been fostered, and therefore what sort of goodbye might be appropriate. The sun was streaming in through the window above, making the stairs are dappled and sunny. Perhaps he took my hand — I cannot think what happened. and he didn’t seem like he was trying to get rid of me at all, in fact, he seemed a little sad that I was leaving.

I said vaguely that we would see each other again, and perhaps exchanged phone numbers.
