I felt like Jasper didn’t quite know how to navigate the social situation and I, for one, didn’t either. He told a few longish stories that were met with an unenthusiastic response. We all walked back to their house and the guy barbequed some stuff in the side yard.

Their apartment was very nice, everything was white, it seemed expensive. We went and sat at the picnic table in the back. The wife and sister were engrossed in a conversation and ignored me. There was something about the food — I wasn’t hungry or it didn’t taste good. The girls were making fun of the boy for keeping on bringing out more and more food even though ostensibly no one was extremely hungry.

I got in a conversation with the man and it felt a lot better than the conversations intermittently I’d been having with the two women who reminded me of everyone I’d gone to high school with. Nevertheless, I enjoyed witnessing their burgeoning female bond and noting the things it seemed to be based on though I felt distinctly that I could not participate in it.

Eventually, Jasper and I walked home and after we got home we relaxed and watched a comedy show — Sarah Silverman probably — some girl making lots of semi-funny jokes that I was engrossed in, thinking about women comics etc. and then we finally settled on watching Trainspotting which was great and I’d never seen it before. We were cuddling on the couch and it was sweet and very cozy even though he seemed to be in a strange position. Eventually we went upstairs and went to bed and made out a little and he ran his hands over my body but didn’t take any of my clothes off. The dog came bounding onto the bed, though, and our excursion ended. In the morning, we said goodbye on the platform between the stairs, unsure of what sort of closeness had been fostered, and therefore what sort of goodbye might be appropriate. The sun was streaming in through the window above, making the stairs are dappled and sunny. Perhaps he took my hand — I cannot think what happened.

and he didn’t seem like he was trying to get rid of me at all, in fact, he seemed a little sad that I was leaving. I said vaguely that we would see each other again, and perhaps exchanged phone numbers.

❦

He said he only liked to have sex doggie style. He told me he’d been sent to a juvenile delinquent high school after causing a lot of trouble in his elementary school. He said he’d been traveling around recently and since he’d graduated from Princeton. He also said that anybody who didn’t go to Princeton or Stanford or Harvard or Yale was a joke.

He said he knew a lot of the cool people in all the cities he visited and that it was hard to find people you actually thought were cool. He said he thought he knew a lot of them that he saw them whenever he visited New York City. Tyler and I confirmed our date midway through my date with Jasper.

Jasper and I were sitting on a bus bench when he called and it took me a little while to figure out who he was. He was supposed to meet me at Brooklyn Park which is a few blocks from my house. I left Jasper’s house early that morning and traveled to the park. First though I went to my house and probably changed.

I think I wore a punkish outfit perhaps the skeleton shirt with my tight black dress. We were supposed to meet on Monday so I left Jasper’s house in the morning and went to the park where we said we’d meet but he was not there and he said since I hadn’t confirmed, he’d gone back to sleep instead of driving the hour to Portland from the farm he was staying at.

He told me it was my fault for not answering his phone call when he’d called that morning, (my phone had died while staying at Jasper’s and I’d bought a new charger so I could see where he was when he didn’t show up as promised.) I said nothing but that I’d wait for him there, and laid down under the swing to overturn handfuls of wood chips and watch a small child play on the slide. \{\{\{ didn’t take full responsibility for it.

He did come eventfully after I laid on the floor of the park for a while and got beer and paper from the store across the street and some other useless things like a mascara that I never used — I don’t think even once. He was a bit shorter than I’d expected though he was handsome.

One of his eyes was swollen shut. We got in his truck and seemed to be arguing already. We couldn’t figure out where to go to eat and eventually, after driving a little, came back to where we’d started and went to this vegan cafe across the street from the park that I’d never been to even though it was blocks from my house.

We got food after deliberating for a while and agreeing to share a bread and cheese plate and I walked around looking at the unique things they had in what was like a vegan grocery store. I sat down and he came to sit next to me.\}\}\} Eventually he appeared towering over me, though he wasn’t actually very tall, only looked so from my position on the ground.

We got into his truck and he told me he’d been hoping I’d show up in something like a long skirt with flowers on it. About to dip onto the highway, I found we’d gotten into an argument about where we should eat, and we turned back — eventually settling on a cafe that was directly across from the park.

While I wandered around the shop looking at all the little things they also carried such as honey sticks and other bee products, he perused the menu on the wall for what seemed like forever. After a while I got tired of that and went to sit down on a chair with a large base.

When the food finally came, the waitress had made some kind of a mistake. Rather than accepting her apology he burned the point into the ground, making sure I and the waitress knew it was not his fault that his food had come with the wrong type of bun. I was confused as to why he’d kept her at our table for so long, enunciating every detail about the bread that wasn’t the kind he’d wanted, until she eventually was set free and dipped back into her shop.

I asked him whether he was trying to hit on her and he said that no, no, she had not been attractive enough for that. I allowed him to walk me back to my house, which was only a few blocks away, and then we sat next to each other on the couch, he explaining to me that he had thought I might be a little high energy for him when we had our phone calls but that he hoped I would be different in person.

He then told me about his last tinder date which had happened in San Francisco with an Asian girl about my age. He had taken her to a park and then home but he didn’t like her and despite her trying to have sex with him, he had refused and gone to his place. He explained the factors which had led to this decision, one of them being that he was tired.

He said he might have been interested in her had she been more chill and not tried to hook up with him. I suggested that perhaps it was because she was much younger than him that he’d found her annoying and that maybe if he dated girls his own age he’d have more things to talk about and more things in common.

I was very tired, having not slept at my house the night before, and we agreed to take a nap together, agreeing first, also, that it would be just a nap. But as we lapsed into silence, he did not keep his promise, opting instead to try something very sinister. Once I realized what he was doing, I stopped him immediately.

He would not apologize. Rather than bading him adieu, I explained to him over and over again why what he had attempted was unacceptable until finally he apologized and we I think we took the nap we’d been planning. We ended up sitting on the steps outside my building. I had been telling him that he was required, whether or not the rest of our date went well, to send me whatever it was he had previously written about art in the past.

He chose that moment to tell me he was not the age he had said he was on his profile but in fact a very different age — one that was three years older than the one he’d previously claimed to be. He said it matter-of-factly — like all the other things he had said which were essentially confessions, his voice didn’t convey any sense of guilt about the situation.

I asked him why he’d chosen that moment to tell me that, and he said it was because he thought the date was going pretty well. He said he was writing a book about what made art good or bad. I said that whether or not we went on more dates, he was required to share his book with me as that I was pretty sure I’d thought about the topic more than him.

He seemed to be very bored about the whole thing. Again, we disagreed about where we wanted to eat. He said he wanted something different and interesting, like a cafe, and I told him I preferred something more traditional, like a diner, or a nice sit down restaurant. I tried to explain that we could lapse into the pretend versions of ourselves but he was not really listening, or could not understand for some reason.

We settled on a bar that had two sides, one just for eating, which was good because I’d forgotten to bring my ID. He wanted to know all about the situation I’d been in the night before. I had lied to him on the phone and told him I was staying with three lesbian girls.

He tried to figure out if they were having me stay with them because they wanted to get with me and asked me questions to determine this. When I mentioned that he was not telling me much about himself, he explained that he did not feel like talking about himself because he had just been on a trip and had had to explain to everyone what he had been doing and he was tired of it.

I had just come from a weird sort of date that lasted for about three days but I concealed that fact by changing the facts a little bit — saying I’d been staying with three lesbians. He seemed to be trying to figure out whether these fictional women had liked my personality, or whether it had been about them trying to get me to sleep with them.

I had to make up more and more “facts” and details about the situation to appease his strange hunger for an understanding of what had happened there at that house where I had been staying for the past few days. I don’t think his findings were conclusive. When the meal was finished, he did not pay for my half of it.

When I mentioned that he was not telling me much about himself, he explained also to me that, because he had just come from a trip in which he had to explain a bunch of things about his life to a lot of people and therefore a lot of times, he was not in the mood to talk about himself, and was content to simply listen to me talk about myself.

He said this as though my feelings in the situation were very unimportant. I cannot imagine why he expected me to be fine with that, though I waited for a further explanation. Perhaps he considered it an honor for me to get to talk about myself the whole time, however, it wasn’t something that was important to me — it was only something that he was interested in.

He didn’t pay for my meal. Afterwards he wanted to go to the supermarket. I wanted to walk but he needed to take his truck. I walked and he met me there in his truck. We stayed until the store closed and just as it was closing, he sent me on a mission to get something he needed (I think it was butter, but there was some confusion about whether it should be salted or not) while he got something else he needed.

We got back in the car and I suggested different things we could do but he was tired and eventually we just went home and went to sleep in my bed. We woke up early, and I was still very tired, but felt slightly sick at having shared a bed with him. but felt slightly uncomfortable at just having shared a bed with someone I did not like in the slightest.

In the morning, he told me that he only found girls that were younger than him attractive. Once again, we were sitting side by side on my couch, this time as I watched him swipe through girls on okcupid. He had his preferences set to girls exactly 22 years of age. He commented on each one, saying they were either ugly, or that they seemed like a slut.

My roommate overheard him and asked him to explain what he meant. Next he argued to me that none of my friends actually wanted to be friends with me and instead that they just wanted to get into my pants. I convinced him that they weren’t trying to get into my pants, citing that none of them had ever tried, even given ample opportunity.

He changed tacts, and said they were most likely using me for my emotional intelligence — my ability to help them understand themselves better. I didn’t think this was true either, and told him their emotions rarely came up and we mostly made up strange scenarios together, and giggled vaguely about them. As we talked, we moved naturally out into the sun outside.

I finished by saying that I didn’t think I had a superior understanding of emotions, and that they seemed more in touch with their emotions at times. Somehow it ended up that I was lying on the grass outside my house looking up at him, as he claimed, moving away from me while shielding his eyes from the sun, that I had basically surrendered the argument to him because I knew he was right.

I didn’t think that was fair, but I saw now the potential damage to his very fragile ego, were I, inevitably, to prove myself right, so I simply discontinued the argument, and told him that winning an argument against him wasn’t my intention. After all, I was certain I was right, since he didn’t know much about any of the friendships I was referencing.

I told him that I didn’t want to make enough points in order to win the argument but rather I was interested in finding out whether he had any interesting reasoning behind what he was saying and he took that to mean that I had given up. I started to explain how that wasn’t true but felt frustrated and explained that he seemed to be changing the terms of our argument so we went inside.

We decided to take a walk around the block and he told me that I had looked better in my pictures. We discussed what our plans for the day were and he said he wanted to go to Powell’s books and that perhaps I could come with him and help him pick up girls. He described how this would work.

We would arrive together. We would scour the store for prospective women that he would be interested in hitting on and when we found one he would make sure she had seen us together. He explained that the main point of my being with him was to avoid seeming like a predator. Once we had been seen together we would then separate and I would strike up a conversation with her, him in close proximity.

At some point he would join the conversation and if it was going well, I should take the cue and let them finish talking so he could take her home. I told him that I didn’t want to do it if that was the end goal, and that I was maybe interested in making friends with girls if that was going to be the end result, but that I didn’t want to be his wingman, and that the main point of my being there was to prove that he wasn’t a predator, when I could not, in good conscience, support that claim.

We went back to my house and he unwrapped the two large pieces of meat that he’d bought at the supermarket, letting the gamey smell waft through our meatless household, then cooked both of them for himself and left without cleaning the grease from the pan. My roommate was none too pleased when he arrived back home, as I hadn’t noticed this trace of his horrible rudeness in the wake of his departure.

He called me the following Saturday while I was at a party and I simply let it go to voicemail.

PAGE ONE

A week after my first date with Gabriel he hadn’t texted and I figured I’d misunderstood his feelings towards me. I was frantically typing on my computer an essay about dating which almost never happened when he texted saying he was in the neighborhood and wanted to come over if it wasn’t too late. After I took a shower and talked excitedly to my roommate, warning him to pretend I wasn’t interested because I was playing it cool, we met and walked to a park where we drank some beer.

He told me that he always felt sad now, when he hung out with his friends that did hard drugs and he avoided them as much as possible. He told me about the last time he’d hung out with them and described how they talked, saying “no they really talk like that.” I told him I’d been on three dates since we’d last seen each other and he said why didn’t I call or text him after our date?

I said he’d mentioned he thought I was crazy on our last date and and he said “you weren’t that crazy.” I said well also it was usually the boy’s job to do that. He said “Wait, you’re saying this is a boy girl thing?” He seemed genuinely surprised. He said he’d been to a party at Reed and taken Molly and I was jealous.

He told me he liked to invite friends from different groups that didn’t know each other to hang out together and then not say much and see how they interacted. He decided to go to the diner on Powell that’s open all night. He ordered something and then I just watched him eat without saying anything.

He asked if I was upset with him. I don’t remember what he had said but I was a little upset with him however I said I was just not feeling talkative. I had gotten really quite drunk and on our walk home I ended up laying on the ground in the middle of the street.

I said I would just stay there even though I just wanted him to be nice to me and help me up. He was kind of leaning away from me but not actually leaving, telling me I was being annoying. Finally he did and we walked back to my place and lay next to each other at the foot of my bed not touching until he wanted to go to sleep and moved up to the pillow part of the bed but when I didn’t follow him he moved down again to be next to me.

I woke up before him and spooned him while he was still sleeping and took a picture of his back and made it a moment on tinder. He offered to get up but he said he wanted to keep sleeping so I went into the living room and talked to my roommates until it was time to meet our other roommates to move into our new house.

After that he developed a strange habit of texting me once a month making it seem like he wanted to hang out and then fading away. I ran into him at the bus stop outside the library in Belmont and we had a very amicable conversation and I told him about my website and that I’d quit dating and he said he’d just come back from a trip to California with his friend and of course we made plans to hang out but never did.

no. 35 · someone i met once

Jacob

He was from Canada.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

he was from canada When I was sad, bored, in the kitchen and wondering blahdy blah what I shud do but omg no that cute boy from tinder wants to see me? I made it seem like I wasn’t concerned and but then asked him to aww a barbecue at the house next door. And I remembered his funny response to whatever I had up at the time.

I didn’t realize he was actually coming; I thought I hadn’t replied enough that he’d forgotten about me. I was talking to Alpha in the kitchen, explaining something on our white board. But then meeting him commanded my attention for the next day and a quarter. I went outside and he was on a skateboard?!

And he’d broken ribs to come meet me is what I interpreted him as saying. I concerned myself with the fact that my casual idea had meant an actual other person having to drive (skateboard) miles and miles in the burning sun and bitter snowy cold. We met outside in the dark and so we couldn’t see each other at first.

I took him the wrong way for a while because I’d been holed up in the kitchen and wanted to walk. All of a sudden we were just like excited and fun having and cute and laughing and having hilarious fun but what the hell the minute after we met but already making jokes. I couldn’t think that a cutesy boy like him would want to come meet me.

He was small but he had the cutest mouth and nose and eyes like a doll and this like huge strip of crowny brown hair that was covering his face. I started thinking about Canada. And that never happens to me. I remember us walking sweet breezy in the moonlight ooh god a sweet face of that tree oh can you count the things that are good about this?

Right away I noticed there was something serious about his playfulness, a hidden undercurrent of a point he was making that I hate and couldn’t take but it was all so sweetly covered in ridiculousness and manners. I brought him over though and alpha was there coming on his conveyor belt to the kitchen to the stairs.

I stood under the bright hostile lights of my kitchen, feeling simultaneously worried he would be disappointed with his date if he’d expected to be attracted to me and caught in this lime light spotlight of the perfect girl that you have to meet because she is so interesting and cool and now she is lightly shifting her weight to feel light to herself, balancing on the cabinet behind her to feel free and to imbue the appropriate amount of displayed discomfort that is appropriate for a first date and meeting in your kitchen that you are supposed to display on a hashtag first date.

It forced me immediately into an “I’m a player” sense of being which I know I will fit into on any tinder occasion. I adopted my “I’m slightly cooler and better than you” proposal accidentally which he seemed to embrace and even take seriously or something; maybe I’m completely wrong. \{In his weds, he kept climbing up to things and the top of the cute narrow mountain he’d created was so narrow it was just a sliver sloping sideways.\} I wanted to hold his hand but I put my hand next to his and then compulsively linked arms with him.

He said like “if we want to do this right we might as well…” So then we held hands the whole way there and it was so nice. Even when we encountered a pole which caused us to unlink, we unanimously voted silently to relink afterwards, and it became almost like an unspoken ritual. We laughed about physics, we laughed about other stuff, we interspersed it with swift observations about rule based systems.

We got lost or something and I brought up that I always got lost and that I was bad at directions and also other logical mental processes like math or no now I remember I told him about dropping out of school and explained it as that I just “couldn’t” do the work cause I like that story, I like telling it to people cause the facts all fit.

He tried to make me feel better by saying that physics is hard. I was shocked that I still had to play that game “I’m stupid” when we’d already bonded over such a range of topics. He was surprised when I mentioned my major was neuroscience. We went to the first bar and went inside and it felt bad and like we were about to have to force conversation or something so we left.

I noticed that from the time that we sat on the wooden bench at pizza on Ainsworth I almost said completely nothing save for when I picked up a phone call. People kept calling me twice that day which means I have to answer in case it’s important. He told me though about being treated at a facility for like seven months.

When he started talking about it he seemed like a smaller boy, telling me about his day at school that had been scary and confusing and he’d come away with a somewhat skewed perception as he was a kid and it helped him to understand things better if they made sense. While he was talking I felt compelled to relate with my own experiences, but I wanted to let him tell me his experience in that way when someone knows they’re telling you something strange that you won’t quite relate to at first.

I wanted him to have the pleasure of knowing he was introducing me to something I had not experienced, because, though I had experienced all the parts that were new to both of us, I still had not had his same experience. I could live vicariously through him, and take myself back to a time when I did not know the horrors of what happened in places such as he spoke of.

He seemed at times to be intellectually smitten with me and at the same time standoffish a little and not trying to suggest that we should kiss more or hold hands more. He kept saying how smitten he was. He kept noting my hilarity and tendency to have ridiculous interesting things to say. He kept saying that together we were having the most interesting conversation anyone had ever had.

I felt uncomfortable that I had told him about my dates not being interested in what I had to say and the swift monopolization of our conversation and also ached to say something but it was against the rules you know? I slipped up and blurted a barrage of blah blah blah about my other dates wondering if I seemed worrisomely detached.

I was, despite myself, interested in the fact that he seemed to be well renowned as a beer connoisseur. I felt like I was learning about a foreign country when he talked about his position. I was in a beautiful space talking to him and he held me aloft with his constant reminders that we were having a good time.

I felt myself judging him in his own eyes which I was but not for the things he thought I was I think. He paid for my drinks and we put our arms around each other on the walk home. At first I wanted to go meet his friends at the hostel downtown because it seemed like an interesting experience.

Then when he was actually trying to plan this I wondered if his initial enthusiasm had turned to boredom or something. The idea was disposed of after a phone call to his hostel mate and we settled on the couch and he explained something to me with an unfitting amount of encouragement on my part and perhaps a tinge of self-awareness about displaying my ability to comprehend complicated things quickly.

On our upstairs part of the night I was on my way downstairs when he made a joke about my undressing which catalyzed taking off my own overalls (I think they were the slutty black ones). It felt as awkward as I thought it would and I slipped myself underneath a blanket. There was some strange closeness like we were really actually close to being actual friends that I felt under the covers.

I watched his head move as he told me about this girl he’d known. He told me all about this girl he’d dated. They’d had chemistry so much chemistry they’d seriously met on chat roulette blah blah blah a pretend pregnancy and then a suicide attempt I didn’t like her from the story but felt bad for the pain she must have suffered and as one of the things that never gets mentioned I wonder why that wasn’t a topic of our conversation.

I couldn’t quite picture why he’d choose to be in such a relationship. He hadn’t presented himself as un-selfconfident and he certainly wasn’t unattractive and he was smart like really wholy smart. His banter was and like did keep going and he did actually know everything that I was saying. Every time I felt that we were about to descend into common philosophical misrepresented platitudes it became cutesy and funny.

There were a few instances of him reflecting on the various ways that words can mean things that almost pissed me off to no end however I was not in the mood for that (for being pissed off). Oh what a strange moment when he suggested that I take medication for my “mental illness.” I settled for believing that once one had discussed with themselves the weighty reasons for weighing themselves down with reasons, their reasons became like a physical object and trying to push them through conversation was inappropriate.

It was unpleasant, it felt like other times, I decided that the fact that he wasn’t wearing a shirt and was in my bed (was he wearing a shirt? It’s unclear now) was reason enough to dismiss the salty charges from my brain with the reasoning I mentioned formed. It didn’t matter. It dissolved into more conversation an we solved it later when he pretended he’d been kidding.

Then it was about this really beautiful tall girl who he knew and actually enjoyed having sex with which I can imagine I would too. I could picture her over him well I tried to because that’s what I was studying that day and his disinterest in sex was interesting to me and this was the counter example so I pictured it.

In the middle of the night, one of my dates called me for the second time so I answered and talked to him in the bathroom for a good half an hour, wondering how Jacob might have cared about that. I slipped back into bed beside him and we resumed cuddling, an easy friendliness between us.

I liked when he said that his friend had changed his pictures that day to ones that he felt were much less good and I agreed. We spent most of the time talking about the strangeness of him not really being interested in having sex with girls. I recall he told me when he met me that he wasn’t interested in tinder to hook up with people blah who says that, what boy?

Or was he saying that cuz he was scared of me trying to hook up with him: my worst fear?

no. 36 · someone i met once

Andrew

A Friday night that started as a photo shoot.
red = words Claude changed or added (0%) · tap text to pause autoscroll
PAGE ONE

It was quite late and I’d been thinking of going out all day, afterall, it was a Friday. Instead I was on the bench in the kitchen playing with my tinder account. Alpha came home at around 10 and we suddenly got into a photo shoot (I was wearing my black overalls and my orange shirt).

I posed in front of the oven, then we moved to the living room for different lighting, then I started taking pictures of him. After we finished, he went upstairs and I left our house, ostensibly to get beer from the 711 which I did, I bought a pack of Total Domination and got into a “conversation” with this guy who was old and attractive and right off the bat told me it was great that I was talking to him and about how people generally considered him a monster and I noticed that he was visibly shaking, he seemed very wired and I even asked him if he was on adderall or something despite the fact that I hate when people ask whether I’m on drugs.

He told me a story after I asked him where he was going, about his friend who he was on the way back from, and how his daughter, while everyone else considered him a monster, had gone right up to him and talked to him and that naturally he’d become friends with the mother and father after a successful interaction such as that.

He told me that I was beautiful, in saying that girls like me never talked to him. I felt conflicted between wanting to end the interaction and wanting to continue it but after it was over I impulsively reached for a reeses pieces and a slurpee. Besides my beer, I ended up buying a mango smoothie for Alpha which was the original mission, plus an ice cream snickers bar which I opened inside of the 711 and proceeded to eat a third of, and then toss into my back pack despite the fact that ice cream has been known to melt.

I made my way from there to Alberta, no particular plan in mind, perhaps simply enjoying having left the house finally. But there are lots of bars on Alberta street and I knew one might hold something fun. I had a large case of beer and certainly couldn’t bring it into any bars, nor was I enjoying carting it around, nor the potential future of carting it around anymore.

I kept changing the way I was carrying it, I’m pretty sure I’d stuffed it into my backpack in case carrying beer was illegal, I couldn’t remember and wasn’t wearing the backpack but holding it out in front of me in different positions. I hightailed it to the Radio Room which is a bar that I like, after carefully hiding the paper bag full of beer behind a drain pipe in front of a yellow building, not fully sure what I intended to do with it after that, noting, though, that the building was yellow so that I could find it if I needed to.

I sat down at the bar at the radio room and ordered a beer and was mind-numbingly pleased with the sensation of alcohol entering my body, I’m pretty sure it was a red beer, as my taste was getting progressively lighter since moving to Portland. After a few moments, a big guy with frizzy brown hair and a band around his forehead sat next to me and started talking to the bartender about how much people had to tip if they forgot their cards at the bar (never closed out).

He seemed to think everyone should tip a lot more — like 20%. He turned to me and asked what I thought. I don’t remember what I said. I’m not fully in favor of tipping a lot, and that is mostly because I ration my money very carefully. He told me that recently he’d been working on his speed reading techniques.

We had a speed reading contest of To Kill a Mockingbird — the sparknotes summary version — of which I set the rules for. After we finished it was unclear how the winner was to be decided. I had a very difficult time staying focused on the material despite my previous confidence about being able to absorb a lot of information quickly and wondered about the relevance of the bar being so loud.

We haphazardly explained what we could remember reading in the book and moved onto a summary of a book by Faulker which was long and ridiculous and I actually remember had something to do with people that have kids and then other people that have more kids and some sort of misunderstanding. I read a lot more of that book than the other one and was somewhat proud to have remembered some of it or even to have comprehended the summary as I was reading it.

After a while we talked about other stuff; I told him I blogged about stuff he said that he was the bassist in a band, and that he was planning to play a show in Eugene the next day. At some point a red-haired boy came up to him and told him that he and some girl were about to leave and my new friend decided he’d stay with me.

He begged me to let him walk me home, promising not to try anything sexual and I didn’t mind at all and pretended like it wasn’t completely ridiculous, him begging me to do this, as though I wasn’t already trying to engineer the situation according to the potential of a similar outcome. Either way, we got hopelessly lost on the way home and I remember collapsing on someone’s grass at some point, (and apparently not remembering to take my backpack with me because I couldn’t find it the next morning and had to pick it up from a nice old couple, who told me I should have a passcode, even though it was precisely the lack of a passcode that had let them contact me, in the first place) and he sitting next to me I think and making out for a moment on the wet grass.

We got to my house, I had to have Alpha let us in which he did and then went straight back to bed. We went upstairs and fell asleep in my bed and in the morning he had to get up early and had to go to Eugene and was awakened by one of his band mates calling him and saying that they had to catch the train so he left.

It was quite late and I’d been thinking of going out all day, afterall, it was a Friday. Instead I was on the bench in the kitchen playing with my tinder account. Alpha came home at around 10 and we suddenly got into a photo shoot (I was wearing my black overalls and my orange shirt). I posed in front of the oven, then we moved to the living room for different lighting, then I started taking pictures of him.

After we finished, he went upstairs and I left our house, ostensibly to get beer from the 711 which I did, I bought a pack of Total Domination and got into a “conversation” with this guy who was old and attractive and right off the bat told me it was great that I was talking to him and about how people generally considered him a monster and I noticed that he was visibly shaking, he seemed very wired and I even asked him if he was on adderall or something despite the fact that I hate when people ask whether I’m on drugs.

He told me a story after I asked him where he was going, about his friend who he was on the way back from, and how his daughter, while everyone else considered him a monster, had gone right up to him and talked to him and that naturally he’d become friends with the mother and father after a successful interaction such as that.

He told me that I was beautiful, in saying that girls like me never talked to him. I felt conflicted between wanting to end the interaction and wanting to continue it but after it was over I impulsively reached for a reeses pieces and a slurpee. Besides my beer, I ended up buying a mango smoothie for Alpha which was the original mission, plus an ice cream snickers bar which I opened inside of the 711 and proceeded to eat a third of, and then toss into my back pack despite the fact that ice cream has been known to melt.

I had a large case of beer and certainly couldn’t bring it into any bars, nor was I enjoying carting it around, nor the potential future of carting it around anymore. I kept changing the way I was carrying it, I’m pretty sure I’d stuffed it into my backpack in case carrying beer was illegal, I couldn’t remember and wasn’t wearing the backpack but holding it out in front of me in different positions.

I hightailed it to the Radio Room which is a bar that I like, after carefully hiding the paper bag full of beer behind a drain pipe in front of a yellow building, not fully sure what I intended to do with it after that, noting, though, that the building was yellow so that I could find it if I needed to.

I sat down at the bar at the radio room and ordered a beer and was mind-numbingly pleased with the sensation of alcohol entering my body, I’m pretty sure it was a red beer, as my taste was getting progressively lighter since moving to Portland. After a few moments, a big guy with frizzy brown hair and a band around his forehead sat next to me and started talking to the bartender about how much people had to tip if they forgot their cards at the bar (never closed out). He seemed to think everyone should tip a lot more — like 20%. He turned to me and asked what I thought. I don’t remember what I said. I’m not fully in favor of tipping a lot, and that is mostly because I ration my money very carefully.

He told me that recently he’d been working on his speed reading techniques. We had a speed reading contest of To Kill a Mockingbird — the sparknotes summary version — of which I set the rules for. After we finished it was unclear how the winner was to be decided. I had a very difficult time staying focused on the material despite my previous confidence about being able to absorb a lot of information quickly and wondered about the relevance of the bar being so loud. We haphazardly explained what we could remember reading in the book and moved onto a summary of a book by Faulker which was long and ridiculous and I actually remember had something to do with people that have kids and then other people that have more kids and some sort of misunderstanding.

I read a lot more of that book than the other one and was somewhat proud to have remembered some of it or even to have comprehended the summary as I was reading it.

After a while we talked about other stuff; I told him I blogged about stuff he said that he was the bassist in a band, and that he was planning to play a show in Eugene the next day. At some point a red-haired boy came up to him and told him that he and some girl were about to leave and my new friend decided he’d stay with me.

He begged me to let him walk me home, promising not to try anything sexual and I didn’t mind at all and pretended like it wasn’t completely ridiculous, him begging me to do this, as though I wasn’t already trying to engineer the situation according to the potential of a similar outcome. Either way, we got hopelessly lost on the way home and I remember collapsing on someone’s grass at some point, (and apparently not remembering to take my backpack with me because I couldn’t find it the next morning and had to pick it up from a nice old couple, who told me I should have a passcode, even though it was precisely the lack of a passcode that had let them contact me, in the first place) and he sitting next to me I think and making out for a moment on the wet grass.

We got to my house, I had to have Alpha let us in which he did and then went straight back to bed. We went upstairs and fell asleep in my bed and in the morning he had to get up early and had to go to Eugene and was awakened by one of his band mates calling him and saying that they had to catch the train so he left.

the ol’ switcheroo My Date with Adam When we were in the house, I really couldn’t take it. I made some jokes at first, as I was putting all my clothes on, after I invited him inside and did nothing to relieve the tension that came from the boundary of my house being dismantled. I went straight back to the desk with the computer wondering if maybe I could just continue writing.

When he was at the door, through the hole in the wood, I could see that he was attractive. His dark brown hair was in front of his face, and he was tall. The whole house seeming like gleaming candy. I laced up my shoes and tossed my jacket on and my backpack over my shoulder and moved around the beautiful wooden floors like I was hot shit.

I told him about my Andrew party as I zipped my jacket. I told him about the phone that only calls Big Bird in the kitchen. He was standing in front of the kitchen table, waiting for me to get all of my stuff and I moved closer to him and he moved away and I moved away.

He hovered next to the kitchen table, almost interacting with the side of the wood and I came over to him and almost to him and almost touched him. He moved away from me though and I moved away too. We met at Beulahland. No we didn’t. He picked me up at my house. My house seeming purple and pink, me bending forward to attach my laces to themselves to each other and to seem like I was occupied and busy – to seem like there was something I was going to do – I was a king masquerading as a queen.

Everything was compiled in the rim of a pair of see-through glasses. Through the royal threshold that led between the dining room and the kitchen I moved, being flippant and adding some politeness as an afterthought. He went with me between the rooms and went with me between the jokes I was making, following at a reasonable distance.

He hovered at the edge of the wooden kitchen table and I came to stand next to him and almost touch him. He flicked himself away to stand slightly to the left so my experiment to see whether I could initiate a physical connection without the preamble of the date had failed. As I made my way around that little space of the kitchen, I began to feel faint.

I overwhelmingly didn’t want to pretend, or make small talk and I wondered if I could simply refuse. I found myself standing on the step above him and was at about his height. I decided to move my head the two inches it would take to reach his. But I didn’t do it. Instead the date went on and he moved back into the kitchen and said resignedly that we should just go to the bar that he had been at.

He led the way outside to his car which was white and notably not falling apart. It seemed like a sports car but I don’t know anything about sports cars. There was something about the front engine that screamed class and that it had taken a little bit of money to buy it. We went inside the car and I note that he had a watch on his wrist and therefore was not exactly a hipster.

It also had hair; so he felt like a man. I was at my desk in the computer room when their appeared a face with brown hair on top of it in the pane of glass that is part of the door, casually. I figured that he was waiting for me to come get him for the date that we’d arranged beforehand so I walked away from my silver computer to open the door for him even though I was still working on the metaphysical theory I’d been engrossed in before this young man came to my house in the middle of the day for what seemed like no particular reason except that there existed a thread of digital communication which had made it occur.

He told me about his job, at evergreen. We got out of the car, we went into the restaurant. I pulled out my wallet to pay for my beer. He said that he had too much money and needed to know what to spend it on. I let him pay for my drink and the drinks turned black then as soon as we got them because they were mine because I hadn’t paid for them.

It wasn’t that he had it was that I hadn’t and so they were black and so things were good. He brought us tall brown bottles of beer that had a red label and white inside of that. We drank them. Pretty fast. I lolled at the table, turning brown – the same color as the dark side of the beer bottles that rolled down from the liquid inside of them.

It seemed unlikely to do anything and while he was in the bathroom I pulled out white note cards that I was in the habit of bringing with me. And we drew ideas for things that we could do that day. We both had a card that said “tell something horrible that happened to you” and his had the addendum that it should not be too terrible.

He said it was because he didn’t want us to start talking about our dead parents. I told him about the night before where I had been stumbling around drunk by myself for literally the entire night. And I’d lost my backpack. Somehow I doubted he’d ever been involved in something so silly, and so stupid, but he told me one night he’d fallen asleep on some grass somewhere outside a bar, woken up after it was closed, and walked to his house and got there when the buses started running.

He said he always sometimes went to sleep in the day as the buses would rumble up outside his window every 20 minutes. He would sometimes scream at them. The cards turning white that we were playing on – the two tinges – the flashes of the perked up white that is to come. He leaves to get us another beer.

The guy at the table in front of us looks at me “It sounds like you guys are having a very interesting conversation. Is it a first date?” I reply yes. When he returned, we began speaking about art. A common interest, it seemed. He began explaining his artistic process involved creating a digital work, and then printing out the picture, but then deleting the digital file.

I understood that this meant that while his work had most of the qualities of being digital, it wasn’t automatically reproducible, and I wondered if this made it more rare for him. In spite of myself, I was impressed with his courage to delete a digital file, and my mind thought of all sorts of alternatives (saving it on a usb, just telling people it was deleted), before I remembered this was the exact point of the work.

I wanted him to know that I knew what he was explaining, without him having to even say it. Stunned that he was still explaining what I already knew I tried to magically ooze myself between his words like bubble syrup explaining that I could say the same thing that he was saying to me to him.

“You see? You get it?” Yes I saw, yes I got it. No oozing allowed. Dear Adam I’m sorry, this is true, this is just what happened. I took a picture of the four bottles of beer laid out in front of me like tracks, explaining things to me through their silence and the longing that was produced by the spaces between them.

I could feel myself slipping, lying down on the fuzzy carpet that was between us, just falling into the ball pit, letting myself get shot at the shooting range, collapsing. I couldn’t explain the silences like I usually could, I let them get to me. Finally we discovered our mutual interest in the movie Donnie Darko, and under the pretense of watching it, returned to his room where we soon found it was impossible.

Instead we were able to find something else to entertain ourselves. The light was growing dim through the large window in his immaculate space, the biggest room in the house, and I lay face down against his pillows, tired from my lack of sleep and he simply lifted my skirt. I might have minded, but he wouldn’t have known, but I didn’t.

Afterwards we made our way into his but instead of getting out as he did, reaching for a white towel hung from the wall, unready for the experience to be over, and still maybe so so tired, I closed my eyes and lay back against the wall of the tub. He came through the space in the curtains and started kissing me and his hands came through as well, through the space the curtains made.

What had just been began again, and He stumbled up from the bed. “Let’s do something. Let’s go get a drink.” Was there a drink on the dresser, or somewhere? I was so tired, it was hard to get out of bed. I was simply delighted that he hadn’t somehow fallen for me and wanted to spend the night sleeping all cuddly and he didn’t already want to dismiss me.

He wanted still to get to know me and we could transition back into the dating phase and that was right, since we’d only been hanging out for a few hours. we got up to go to the bar. We went to Swift. We talked to his roommate briefly before we left and Adam talked to him about meeting us there.

Swift was a warm bar, and all the colors were in oranges. There were lots of people lolling around everywhere, starting to do things with each other, all sorts of things. I walked into the bar with Adam, and Adam told me to stand by our table so I could save it for us. Perhaps because I’d offered to pay for my drink at the beginning of the date, he seemed then willing to buy all sorts of other things for me, not least of all was the burger, the cocaine, the coffee, and some more drinks. they talked about going skiing on mount hood.

I sort of leaned my head down on Adam a little bit, but just for a second because he didn’t reciprocate at all, didn’t grab my head and pull it towards him. The man at the table next to us went away from his girl. When I fell asleep on the couch, they left and went to buy the cocaine. I was curious what had happened when I fell asleep. one of them said “Cocaine. ayyyyne.” (I asked Alex the next day. Other things that were added to that category were the girl he’d talked about who he hadn’t described as seeming to care about him that much but had seemed to rope him into different things. Also him paying for everything for me — all the cocaine. I had tried not to take too much advantage of him.

I was well aware of myself manipulating my patterns or certainly seeming to manipulate or potentially manipulate my patterns in regards to recounting my previous experience in dating. The same thrill of truth or dare — the invitation where the reward far exceeds the vulnerability it takes to make the invitation.) He placed the plastic white pizza table in front of me on the coffee table. “It needs chairs.” “What?” “It needs chairs.” He started ripping up one of the note cards. My Date with Adam

When we were in the house, I really couldn’t take it. I made some jokes at first, as I was putting all my clothes on, after I invited him inside and did nothing to relieve the tension that came from the boundary of my house being dismantled. I went straight back to the desk with the computer wondering if maybe I could just continue writing.

When he was at the door, through the hole in the wood, I could see that he was attractive. His dark brown hair was in front of his face, and he was tall.

The whole house seeming like gleaming candy. I laced up my shoes and tossed my jacket on and my backpack over my shoulder and moved around the beautiful wooden floors like I was hot shit.

I told him about my Andrew party as I zipped my jacket. I told him about the phone that only calls Big Bird in the kitchen. He was standing in front of the kitchen table, waiting for me to get all of my stuff and I moved closer to him and he moved away and I moved away.

He hovered next to the kitchen table, almost interacting with the side of the wood and I came over to him and almost to him and almost touched him. He moved away from me though and I moved away too.

We met at Beulahland. No we didn’t. He picked me up at my house. My house seeming purple and pink, me bending forward to attach my laces to themselves to each other and to seem like I was occupied and busy – to seem like there was something I was going to do – I was a king masquerading as a queen. Everything was compiled in the rim of a pair of see-through glasses.

Through the royal threshold that led between the dining room and the kitchen I moved, being flippant and adding some politeness as an afterthought.

He went with me between the rooms and went with me between the jokes I was making, following at a reasonable distance.

He hovered at the edge of the wooden kitchen table and I came to stand next to him and almost touch him. He flicked himself away to stand slightly to the left so my experiment to see whether I could initiate a physical connection without the preamble of the date had failed.

As I made my way around that little space of the kitchen, I began to feel faint. I overwhelmingly didn’t want to pretend, or make small talk and I wondered if I could simply refuse. I found myself standing on the step above him and was at about his height. I decided to move my head the two inches it would take to reach his. But I didn’t do it. Instead the date went on and he moved back into the kitchen and said resignedly that we should just go to the bar that he had been at.

He led the way outside to his car which was white and notably not falling apart. It seemed like a sports car but I don’t know anything about sports cars. There was something about the front engine that screamed class and that it had taken a little bit of money to buy it.

We went inside the car and I note that he had a watch on his wrist and therefore was not exactly a hipster. It also had hair; so he felt like a man.

I was at my desk in the computer room when their appeared a face with brown hair on top of it in the pane of glass that is part of the door, casually. I figured that he was waiting for me to come get him for the date that we’d arranged beforehand so I walked away from my silver computer to open the door for him even though I was still working on the metaphysical theory I’d been engrossed in before this young man came to my house in the middle of the day for what seemed like no particular reason except that there existed a thread of digital communication which had made it occur.

He told me about his job, at evergreen. We got out of the car, we went into the restaurant. I pulled out my wallet to pay for my beer. He said that he had too much money and needed to know what to spend it on. I let him pay for my drink and the drinks turned black then as soon as we got them because they were mine because I hadn’t paid for them. It wasn’t that he had it was that I hadn’t and so they were black and so things were good.

He brought us tall brown bottles of beer that had a red label and white inside of that. We drank them. Pretty fast. I lolled at the table, turning brown – the same color as the dark side of the beer bottles that rolled down from the liquid inside of them.

It seemed unlikely to do anything and while he was in the bathroom I pulled out white note cards that I was in the habit of bringing with me. And we drew ideas for things that we could do that day. We both had a card that said “tell something horrible that happened to you” and his had the addendum that it should not be too terrible.

He said it was because he didn’t want us to start talking about our dead parents. I told him about the night before where I had been stumbling around drunk by myself for literally the entire night. And I’d lost my backpack. Somehow I doubted he’d ever been involved in something so silly, and so stupid, but he told me one night he’d fallen asleep on some grass somewhere outside a bar, woken up after it was closed, and walked to his house and got there when the buses started running. He said he always sometimes went to sleep in the day as the buses would rumble up outside his window every 20 minutes. He would sometimes scream at them.

The cards turning white that we were playing on – the two tinges – the flashes of the perked up white that is to come.

He leaves to get us another beer. The guy at the table in front of us looks at me “It sounds like you guys are having a very interesting conversation. Is it a first date?” I reply yes.

When he returned, we began speaking about art. A common interest, it seemed. He began explaining his artistic process involved creating a digital work, and then printing out the picture, but then deleting the digital file. I understood that this meant that while his work had most of the qualities of being digital, it wasn’t automatically reproducible, and I wondered if this made it more rare for him.

In spite of myself, I was impressed with his courage to delete a digital file, and my mind thought of all sorts of alternatives (saving it on a usb, just telling people it was deleted), before I remembered this was the exact point of the work.

I wanted him to know that I knew what he was explaining, without him having to even say it.

Stunned that he was still explaining what I already knew I tried to magically ooze myself between his words like bubble syrup explaining that I could say the same thing that he was saying to me to him.

“You see? You get it?” Yes I saw, yes I got it. No oozing allowed.

PAGE ONE

Impulsively I asked a boy if I could stay at his house without meeting him. It was that or spend the night at my new “life-long friend” that I’d met on Craigslist that day, who wanted me to move into the closet-sized, window-less room upstairs almost as much as he wanted to lecture me on how being a vegan wasn’t really a choice as much as a lifestyle.

I arranged to meet my date at a stand up comedy club in downtown after notifying him that I would need to spend the night at his house. I took the bus there and texted lots of people while I was on it, including my dad I think. I arrived and he was sitting near the entrance in a tall canvas chair and neglected to interact with me besides waving me over.

His awkwardness and the fact that he was not very attractive made me disappointed in myself. I texted people more during the show, namely my mom. Which guy? The one who’d read all of his jokes out of a lined notebook he’d set on the stool next to him. Which ones had been funny (none), and how better to present them, down to microscopic details like word choice. in which a performer singled us out for not laughing and I defended a girl whose birthday it was after after her set the MC made a joke about liking the fact that girls don’t enjoy blow jobs.

One disappointingly hellish stand-up comedy show later and we were outside analyzing, with future Louis CK himself, microscopic details of his own jokes. It was my fault as I had initiated the interaction by asking him to “explain” his last joke which hadn’t made sense to myself or anyone in the audience. He mistook my plea which was really a jab as a request from an adoring fan, and explained, to my date but not to me, this joke plus numerous other ones that we didn’t ask for.

If there’s ever a time I regret not punching someone in the face…but I digress. Myself, this moron, my disappointingly unattractive OkCupid date, and my disappointingly unattractive okcupid date’s roommate Chris, who I mistakenly called Brian a little over three times went outside to watch as he “did a quick run down,” of the microscopic details of every joke he had told, pilfering the air space with the squeaks from the skateboard he was allowing to lifelessly move beneath him.

I went inside to use the bathroom and while peeing, thought up an excellent joke to add to the mix. It goes: “If I had a quarter for every time people ignored me at the end of a comedy show, then I would probably patent the technology that enables me to receive money every time an arbitrary event occurs and make a living wage off of that.”

Alex the up-and-coming soon-to-be-very-famous monotone comic gave me a pity laugh, then told me it was because he didn’t want it to be awkward and also he wanted to encourage nubes. I thought of another joke and told it to them, this one even more blatantly about being ignored and explained both of them to my date sort of quietly.

After this my date, who got it, and I, started to get along pretty well and made lots of jokes together on our way to the car together, and in the car together, in which I sat in the back seat so that his roommate, fat, actually-Brian Chris could sit in the front. His house was extremely far away and I passed the spot where Thomas and I had met on the side of the road that one night next to the mini mart and the bus stop.

When we arrived at his house, two more unattractive nerdy boys emerged from the woodwork — I mean came out of the kitchen. One was small and Indian, the other had a ginger afro and lots of acne. They were gearing up to play Mario Kart together on the one piece of furniture in their house, which was a large purple couch opposite the TV.

There was absolutely nothing on the walls, and the whole house smelled like pizza. I joked that they had slightly too much furniture to my date who was standing near the doorway still (I had walked to the fold out table to put my yellow legal pad down and other stuff) except he didn’t understand what I was saying and was confused and said that he didn’t think there was too much furniture, in fact he didn’t think there was much furniture at all.

I had to explain it to him. I wrote down some thoughts I’d been thinking while he talked to his roommates sorta, and then he offered me a thermos which it turned out contained a two week old vodka cranberry that tasted like vinegar because vinegar is what you get when a beverage is left sitting long enough to ferment.

He told me the story of how he’d “lost” his drink, and then it had turned up again about three days — no maybe more like a week — later, and then he’d put it into the thermos I now held in my faintly quivering hand. I excused myself to try and vomit and he laughed nervously, saying he didn’t think alcohol could go bad.

Before I had tasted it, I searched the entire kitchen for some sort of drinking apparatus other than the thermos, more formally known as a cup. There were none, the last thing on the shelf you might consider a mini-cup (also known as a shot glass), which I poured a small amount of while he was in the other room with his friends doing something, and filled it and drank some and left the tiny glass near the sink since I wasn’t going to drink the rest of it.

I asked him what it was and he said “vodka cranberry” and I said there might be vinegar in it to which he replied that he didn’t think so. He wanted to show me his basement where he and his roommates put on a weekly podcast show so I went down with him and we looked at all the lego things he had there and I asked if I could play the drums and he said it was fine and that one of the advantages of living so far away from everything was that it was permissable to make loud noises even in the middle of the night so I gave the drums a few loud thwacks and then turned away from them and put the drumsticks back, resting on one of the round platforms.

We went back upstairs after I made fun of him for offering me an expired drink and he refused to believe that there could actually be vinegar in it and said it tasted fine. He led me into his bedroom but I lingered outside, asking awkwardly what he did for work so that he was forced to pose half-leaning on the side of the refrigerator.

He worked at Subway, he said, which was why he only had eleven dollars in his wallet and couldn’t afford to take me anywhere where the spending of money was encouraged and/or required. I saw the back of Gabriel’s head when I went to the Hot Cake House and called “Gabriel” twice but he didn’t turn around. So I went to his table where he was standing looking around being confused and tapped him twice on the forearm and when he turned around I started giggling in his face, except I was just a tiny bit below him, but just a tiny bit and babbling at him.

He hasn’t really talked so I say “what are you doing?” and he says “Oh, I just spilled beer on myself” and I see that there is a can of Tecate hanging out next to the one table leg and that, yeah, his butt is kinda wet. But he’s not really doing anything, he’s turning slightly in a few directions and just looking very confused.

So after I said whatever I said, which I don’t remember, I went back to my seat with the other guy. “No, we have to go back, I want to punch him in the face.” I wasn’t intending at all to punch him in the face, but I thought that might be interesting enough for him to want to go back.
